#### The §0 checker could not read an alternation

The new row's check, `grep -rho 'a\|b' … | wc -l` → 5, reported `tree
says 0` from `ns-status-check` while the same line printed 5 in a shell.
`ns_ledger.rows` turns every `\|` in a cell back into `|`, because a
table cell escapes its column separator that way and the checker cannot
tell that escape from a basic-regex alternation - so the pattern ran as a
LITERAL pipe and matched nothing.  Six rows already in §0 were written
that way, every one expecting **0**: D11's two, the home-module row's,
`family_symbol`'s, `qualify_symbol_sym_home`'s, the import-alias row's.
Each held whatever the tree grew back.  The pair, with the roster and
the checker held at `6e32022e` and one `set_home_module` mention added
to `sema/lambda_synth.cryo`:

* the OLD checker over the OLD §0: `ns-status-check: OK -- 183 §0
  row(s) … match the tree`;
* the rows rewritten as one `-e` per alternative (no pipe, and the same
  command copied whole as run): `DRIFT … §0 says 0 / tree says 1`;
* the NEW checker over the OLD §0: `8 §0 check(s) cannot report drift as
  written`, each named `UNUSABLE CHECK`.

`-E` is not the fix: the checker would read `a|b` as an alternation, and
a reader copying the row's `a\|b` whole would run a literal pipe under
`-E` too.  D2's `-cE '(Type\|Value\|Function)'` was that shape and is
rewritten the same way.  The rule lives in `ns-status-check.py`
(`PIPED_PATTERN`): a grep whose quoted pattern carries a pipe is refused
by name, before it runs.

`scripts/ns-guard-selftest.py` carries the rule as two cases (a piped
row refused as `UNUSABLE CHECK` - by that text, since the row also
drifts and a drift refusal would pass the case for the wrong reason - and
its `-e` twin allowed).  The self-test was RED before either case
existed: `bd0c8580` raised the checker's row floor to 28 and left the
fixture at 26, so every allow-case had been refused since 2026-09-10,
and nothing ran it.  The fixture sits at the floor now, `make
guard-selftest` runs it, and CI's ubuntu job runs that after
`ns-status-check`; 14 cases, refusals and allowances both.

Gates: `check-fast` OK (`lane-check` unmoved, no lookup surface changed); `guard-selftest` 14 of 14; `test-census` OK (2,122 unit, 183 compile-fail,
**53** of 56 projects on this host, the new one among them); `lsp-check`
OK (264 modules, 0 errors); `cross-check` OK (243 compiler modules);

### 8.206 D5 TAKEN: modules and types share one namespace, the collision is E0205 where the pair is completed, and the module-vs-type adjudication is deleted with the cursor lane it fed - 2026-09-16

#### The ruling, read against the resolver's own scoping

§8.130 records the ruling as Rust's model - `mod x` beside `struct x` is
E0428 - and §8.170 paraphrased it as "refused at `type struct Buffer`" for
`namespace Gpu::Buffer;` declaring that struct.  In Rust those are two
different programs: `mod buffer { struct buffer }` is legal, because a
module's name is not in scope inside itself.  In this resolver it is.
`CompilationContext::modules_written_as` counts a module as spelled by any
whole-segment suffix of its namespace when the module is the writer's own
(`cand_ns.id == use_ns.id`), imported, the whole name, or the prelude's -
so inside `Gpu::Buffer`'s file the one segment `Buffer` already names the
module, and a `type Buffer` declared there is a second owner of one name
in one scope.  That is the E0428 shape under Cryo's scoping, and it is
what §8.130's instrument counted ("namespace leaf spelled like a type
declared in the same file"): three survivors, all in `tests/`.  The
importer's side is the same pair completed from the other end: `import
Gpu::Vertex;` makes `Vertex` spell the module in the importing scope, and
a `type Vertex` declared or imported there is the second owner.  Both are
"a module and a type carrying the same name", both are refused as the
ordinary redeclaration error, E0205, at the entry that completed the pair.
Written down as `docs/cryo.md` §14.6 and §4 rule 5 here.

#### The mechanism

`NameResolver::refuse_module_type_collisions`, once per module scope at
the end of its walk - after the imports are bound, since either side can
complete the pair.  For each entry of the scope that names a type
(`symbol_names_type`: declared as one, or an import whose target is one,
resolved through the owning module's export set as every qualified path
is), `modules_written_as(name, ns)` says whether the name spells a
reachable module; failing that, `<ns>::<name>` is asked of the module
graph directly - `namespace A;` declaring `type N` beside a module
`A::N` shares its canonical name whether or not `A` imports it.  Probed
before the corpus with one project per shape under the built compiler:
the own-leaf declaration (`src/widget.cryo:2:1`), a declaration under an
imported module's leaf (`main.cryo:3:1`), an import of a type under an
imported module's leaf (`main.cryo:4:1`), the sibling (`main.cryo:3:1`),
every one E0205 naming the module; a legal control - module `Buffer`
declaring `Handle`, `Buffer::make` its function, `Buffer::USAGE` its
constant - exits 7.

Name resolution is fatal per module, so a program with two collisions in
two files reports the first module's; the two pinned shapes are two
projects for that reason.

#### The population, measured with the refusal live and the tests untouched

`corpus2.sh m4` over the six halves: **1** failing half,
`module_type_name_collision`'s test half (`src/gpu/buffer.cryo:9:1`), and
the unit suite refusing to compile at `tests/lang/static_method_value.cryo:30`
(`make test exit=2`).  A third is invisible to that run and was found by
building it directly: `namespace_gate_methods`, a `compile_fail` project
expecting E0240, now failed at `src/handler.cryo:9:1` with E0205 instead -
the half reports a wanted non-zero exit and nothing else.  Those three
are exactly §8.130's three; `compiler/src`, `stdlib`, `tools/CryoLSP` and
`examples/` hold none, which the compiler's own build, `lsp-check` and
`cross-check` say as well as the structural argument does.

* `namespace_gate_methods`: the module renamed `Handling`; its trait
  `Handler` and its E0240 are the test, and the collision was incidental.
* `static_method_value.cryo`: the type renamed `Emitter`.  Its three tests
  - a static taken as a value from inside the type's body and from
  outside, a module function taken the same way - are the coverage worth
  keeping; the collision was the file's premise and is refused now.
* `module_type_name_collision`: `collect` → `compile_fail`, E0205 at
  `src/gpu/buffer.cryo:9:1`, its `tests/` half deleted (it exercised the
  adjudication).  `module_type_import_collision` is new, E0205 at
  `src/main.cryo:8:1` for the declaration-under-imported-leaf shape;
  `E0205_type_named_as_its_module` is the single-file negative.

#### Deleted, in the same commit

* `check_module_type_collision` (114 lines): the E0154 for a member BOTH
  the module and its same-leaf type declared.  It adjudicated a pair the
  name layer now refuses at its declaration.
* `stamp_module_scope`'s module-owns-member probe: a segment bound in
  scope as a type answered type-relative UNLESS a same-spelled module
  owned the next segment.  A segment bound as a type is type-relative.
  Its import-target lookup and the new check's are one helper,
  `symbol_names_type`.
* `scope_owner_key`'s cursor lane (`resolve_scoped_at` between
  `spec_owner` and the stamp; §8.170 measured 1,974,585 answers serving
  the one refused shape) and, with their last reader gone,
  `CompilationContext::resolve_scoped` and `resolve_scoped_at`.
* `resolve_scope_call`'s cross-kind trying.  The ladder asked the static
  method, variant, module function and C-import stores in turn for every
  segment; §8.195 measured the stamp deciding every answer but two, the
  refused shape's `Buffer::make`.  A `Def` segment now asks the module
  store alone; any other segment - a type, a primitive, a type parameter,
  a C-import alias, which the name layer stamps type-relative because the
  alias is a namespace symbol rather than a graph module (§9 Q2) - asks
  the three type-owned stores.  One more `require_scope_res` door (D23,
  13 → 14 mentions).

`bare_alts` and `DeclarationIndex::resolve_qualified_scoped` are NOT
deleted: with the cursor lane gone the compiler has no reader of either,
but `tools/CryoLSP`'s completion handler resolves a typed leaf through

### 8.207 D19 TAKEN: a bare allocator leaf is E0202 naming its declarers; the intrinsic's bare key, its four durability guards and codegen's leaf-spelled allocation are deleted - 2026-09-16

#### The one bare path, and what held it

`callee_family` answered a `Pending` callee - a bare name the name layer
bound to nothing - through `intrinsic_owner_of(leaf)`, the record of
which `intrinsic function` declared that leaf.  That record was written
by `register_intrinsic_function_type`, which also registered the
intrinsic under its bare leaf in every function table (return, signature,
mangled slot, overload entry, `bare_alts`) and dropped an `extern "C"`
twin's entry from the leaf's overload index so the leaf "dispatcher" saw
the intrinsic alone; four guards in `register_function`,
`register_function_type_owned`, the overload restamp and
`register_mangled_name` then refused any later same-leaf write, so that
`alloc::heap::free` could not rebind a bare `free` program-wide.  All of
it existed so that `free(p)` written in a module declaring no `free`
would bind SOMETHING, and which something depended on the link: the
intrinsic where the guards held, `heap::free` - which reads a segment
header and aborts on a libc pointer - where they did not
(`bare_intrinsic_priority.cryo`'s premise).  D19 says the spelling names
nothing, as every other undeclared bare name does.

#### Built

* `callee_family`'s unanswered arm returns no family.  The call then
  falls to `resolve_direct_call`'s E0202, which now carries a note when
  the leaf is a free function of some module:
  `collect_module_declarers_of_leaf` walks the overload keys for
  `<module>::<leaf>` where `<module>` is in the graph (a type's static
  shares the key shape and is excluded), and the note names each and its
  suffix spelling - for `free`: `std::core::intrinsics`, `std::ffi::libc`,
  `std::alloc::heap`; write `intrinsics::free`, `libc::free` or
  `heap::free`, or import it.  Data-driven, so `malloc` names two and
  `realloc` three, and a leaf nothing declares keeps the did-you-mean.
* `note_intrinsic(leaf, owner)` replaces `register_intrinsic_function_type`:
  the leaf → declaration record alone, read by codegen's
  `callee_is_intrinsic` to tell a pin to the intrinsic from a pin to a
  function sharing its leaf.  Type resolution's intrinsic arm registers
  the declaration under its qualified name only; the bare
  `register_function`, `register_name_mapping`, `register_mangled_name`
  and `register_overload_mangled_owned` writes and the four durability
  guards are deleted (`decl_index.cryo` -87 lines net).
* Codegen's synthesized allocation (`expr_ops.cryo`, three `malloc`
  sites and the `delete` rung behind the `std::alloc::allocator::free`
  shim) names `std::core::intrinsics::malloc` / `::free` - the family
  the intrinsic registers as - instead of the leaf the deleted bare
  registration supplied.  `core/intrinsics.cryo`'s header no longer
  claims the three declarations exist to hold the bare leaf: they are
  the allocator a program without `std::alloc::allocator` names.

#### Population

`grep -rn -E '(^|[^:A-Za-z_.])(free|malloc|realloc)\(' --include=*.cryo
stdlib compiler/src tools examples tests runtime`, minus definitions,
comments and `.method(` forms: **13** bare calls.  Legal under D19, the
writing module declaring the leaf: `stdlib/ffi/libc.cryo` 3 (extern
block), `stdlib/alloc/heap.cryo` 1 (`public function free`), and the two
E0453 negatives' 4 - each declares `malloc`/`free` in its own `extern
"C"` block, which the previous handoff had counted as bare-with-no-
declaration; they are not.  Refused: `tests/lang/bare_intrinsic_priority.cryo`'s
5, one file, which asserted the bare bind ("must keep binding the
intrinsic").  It is `E0202_bare_allocator_leaf.cryo` now, three
annotated calls, the note checked by hand.  `compiler/src` holds none
and `stdlib` none but the four declared ones, which is what the
compiler's own build says.

#### Gates

`check-fast` OK; `test-census` OK (2,120 unit, 185 compile-fail, 54 of
57 projects on this host); `lsp-check` OK (264 modules, 0 errors);
`cross-check` OK (243 compiler modules, the freestanding runtime tiers
compiling `new` through the renamed rung); objects
(`.objcmp/m6-objcmp.out`): **examples 0 of 1,126, tests 0 of 2,333**.
`ns-status-check` 201 rows.

### 8.208 D20 TAKEN: an import path the graph holds no module under is E0502 at the import, measured at zero first - 2026-09-16

#### What the shape is

A path naming no FILE was already refused at discovery (E0500, `cannot
find module`), plain or braced.  What survived was the path the loader
resolves to a file whose namespace is spelled otherwise: `import
core::option;` reaches `stdlib/core/option.cryo`, the graph registers
`std::core::option`, and `process_import`'s `find_module_index` misses -
so the import bound nothing, and as a plain `import M;` (D7: it binds no
names by design) said nothing.  The braced form of the same path reached
`refuse_unoffered_import` per entry with a message about a module that
does not exist.  A module gated off this OS (`![config(linux)]` on
Windows) is NOT this shape: the graph holds it, empty, and the import
names it.

#### Measured first

The refusal was landed as a `SHADOW\tIMPORT-UNKNOWN` line first and
run over the six halves (`corpus2.sh m7`: **0** lines, 0 failing halves)
and, since `cross-check.py` keeps only error lines, over the four
Linux-target builds by hand (`runtime`, `stdlib`, `compiler`,
`tools/CryoLSP` with `--target=x86_64-pc-linux-gnu`: **0** lines, every
build exit 0).  Control: a scratch project writing `import core::option;`
printed the line and compiled; one importing a `![config(linux)]` module
on this host printed nothing and compiled.  So the population is zero
and the instrument can report non-zero.

#### Built

`refuse_unknown_module_import`, ahead of every style in `process_import`:
E0502 `` `core::option` is not a module's name ``, labelled at the import,
with a help naming every module the path is a whole-segment suffix of
(`Resolver::ns_written_as` over the graph) - the mistake the shape comes
from is writing where an import wants the whole name the abbreviation a
qualifier is allowed.  The braced form no longer reaches its entries
against a missing offering.  Pinned by `E0502_import_names_no_module`.

### 8.209 D21 TAKEN: an unknown type in a body annotation is E0203 where it is written, the reporter walks the whole annotation by stamp, and `1 as Nope` no longer compiles - 2026-09-16

#### Four answers to one question

Under `8ad52d6a`, a type declared nowhere was reported four ways by
position: a declaration's annotation `const x: Nope` was E0203 from type
resolution's gate; `sizeof(Nope)` was E0900 at codegen (the pinned
refusal of an operand nothing decided); `Array<Nope>` in a local's
annotation was E0636 at codegen against `Array::new`, the instantiation
having failed silently; and **`1 as Nope` compiled and ran** - the cast
target unresolved, the cast emitted as nothing, exit 1.  `docs/cryo.md`
§12.2 already said "a name that exists nowhere is an error in every
position, expression and type-argument positions included: `sizeof(Nope)`,
`1 as Nope` and `Array<Nope>` are refused".  The spec was normative and
the tree was the defect.

Two gaps, one mechanism each:

* Sema resolves three annotations in bodies itself - a local's, the
  `sizeof`/`alignof` operand's (`resolve_layout_operand`), the cast
  target's (`resolve_cast`) - and on failure left the slot unset with no
  diagnostic.  Type resolution's own body walk covers locals in
  non-generic bodies only.
* The reporter's `extract_unresolved_named` PEELED to the head: for
  `Tagged<bool>` it reached `Tagged`, which resolves, so
  `annotation_failure_is_certain` was written to fire on a bare `Named`
  alone and to leave every wrapped form unreported ("those wrapped forms
  are left to their existing handling" - which was nothing).

#### Measured first

The three sema sites printed a `SHADOW` line per failed resolution with
the first name in the annotation the name layer had NOT stamped, or
`<stamped>` when every name was placed, and the walk's mode.  Over the
six halves (`corpus2.sh m9`, 6,655 lines): unstamped names **2**, both
`sizeof_undeclared_type`'s `Nope` (once per sema walk, pre- and
post-mono); stamped-but-unresolvable **6,653**, every one a LOCAL's
annotation (3,937 in the symbolic walk, 2,401 in the post-mono re-check,
308 concrete pre-mono, 7 symbolic post-mono), none a `sizeof` or a cast.
Control: the three probe programs printed `sizeof Nope`, `cast Nope`,
`local Nope` respectively.

The 6,653 are a FINDING, not this entry's: a local whose annotation the
type layer cannot resolve while every name in it is placed - a
projection, a form reduced later, an annotation the substituter did not
rewrite - and sema proceeds on the initializer's type.  Unrowed; nothing
here changes what they do.

#### Built

* `extract_unresolved_named` is a walk over the WHOLE annotation by
  stamp - pointers, references, arrays, tuples, function shapes, generic
  base and arguments - returning the first `Named` leaf with no answer
  and no pre-resolved type.  A placed name is not the failure;
  `Tagged<bool>` names `bool`.  `annotation_failure_is_certain` asks it
  (`top_level_named` is deleted); the deferred forms it must not fire on
  (`typeof`, `implement Trait`, a projection) hold no unplaced name.
* Every branch of `emit_undefined_type` that reports a leaf marks it
  `Res::Err` afterwards, so the leaf is placed for the next asker: type
  resolution's body walk and sema's pre- and post-mono walks ask the same
  annotation, and one unknown name is one diagnostic.
* Sema's three sites call `refuse_unresolved_body_annotation` on
  failure: the runner's certainty predicate, then its reporter -
  E0203 at the leaf's span with the did-you-mean, or E0240 with the
  import to add, exactly as a declaration gets.

The default-parameter half of D21 was already the name layer's:
`declare_generics` stamps a parameter's default annotation in the
declaring file (§8.193), and §8.204 found the use-site re-homing that
stood beside it read by nothing.

### 8.212 D24 MEASURED: the trait registry's leaf key loses an impl in one shape, one program holds it, and the re-key is Jake's call - 2026-09-16

#### What was measured, and where

D24 asks for the trait half shadowed whole before it is ruled on.
§8.194 measured one reader (193,199 answers, 9 disagreeing).  This
entry instruments the two places a leaf key can differ from an identity
key at all:

* **Registration.**  `register_trait_impl` and `register_trait_impl_typed`
  overwrite an existing `(leaf, target)` entry ("latest impl wins").  An
  overwrite by a block whose `TypeAnnotation::trait_identity` differs
  from the entry's is an impl the table LOSES; an overwrite by the same
  identity is the same node registered under a second key (stage 3
  under the written target, type resolution under the canonical one, a
  placed clone under its specialization).
* **Readers holding an identity.**  `type_implements_trait` and
  `type_satisfies_opaque_bound` receive the bound's identity
  (`TraitRef::identity()`, a stamped annotation) and hand
  `dispatch_leaf(...)` to `resolve_trait_impl_for_type`; the block the
  leaf finds carries its own identity, compared to the one meant.  The
  Drop/Copy queries and the operator desugars (`Add`, `Index`, `Deref`)
  pass a LEAF by design - an operator names "the `Add` implemented for
  this type", whatever module declares it - and are a different
  question (coherence, not identity); they were logged with the
  well-known identity where one exists and every one agreed.

Over the six halves (`corpus2.sh m15`, 1,047,373 lines, 0 failing
halves, `.objcmp/d24-measurement-lines.txt`):

| site | answers | differ |
|---|---:|---:|
| overwrite, bare table, same identity | 4,034 | - |
| overwrite, typed table, same identity | 206 | - |
| overwrite, typed table, **different identity** | **1** | `trait_leaf_dispatch`: `(Render, Shape)`, `Alpha::Render`'s block replaced by `Omega::Render`'s |
| bound check (`type_implements_trait`) | 84,514 | **3**, all `trait_leaf_dispatch`: a `T: TraitLeafDispatch::Alpha::Render` bound answered by `Omega::Render`'s block |
| opaque-bound check | 6 | 0 |
| Drop typed / bare, `wellknown("Drop")` meant | 795,165 | 0 |
| other readers, identity meant | 5,378 | 0 |
| other readers, leaf meant (operator traits) | 158,066 | not a disagreement |

#### What the one shape is

Two traits sharing a leaf, both implemented for one type - `Alpha::Render`
and `Omega::Render` for `Shape` - collapse to one table entry under
`(leaf, target)`, so `traits_implemented_by(Shape)` offers `Render`
once and `lookup_trait_impl(Render, Shape)` hands back whichever impl
registered last.  A bound `T: Alpha::Render` checked against `Shape` is
then answered by `Omega`'s block: satisfied here because neither impl
carries a where-clause, and a type implementing ONLY `Omega::Render`
would satisfy an `Alpha::Render` bound the same way.  The project passes
today because sema's concrete-receiver binder reads the type's folded
method list (both impls' methods, each with its own `origin_trait`) and
never the registry.  §8.194's 9 were this project's 6 and 3 `LeafDispatchA::Pulse`
heads that the typed table, keyed by the target's canonical name since
§8.199, no longer collapses.

Nothing in `compiler/src`, `stdlib`, `tools/CryoLSP`, `examples/` or the
unit suite holds the shape.

#### What is not decided here

Re-keying the trait half by identity would make both impls visible to
every registry reader and answer a bound by the trait it names.  It is
one program in the tree and it is Jake's call, by the ruling; the
previous re-key was backed out for being decided rather than measured,
and this is the measurement.  The instrument is not in the tree: it was
reverted after the run, and this entry rides with the next code commit
rather than alone.

### 8.213 D2 and D9 TAKEN: `Namespace::Function` folds into `Value`, and a type declaration takes a `where` clause - 2026-09-16

#### D2: two namespaces, as Rust has

`Namespace` is `Type` and `Value`.  `Value` accepts every value-bearing
symbol kind - variable, parameter, constant, enum variant, function,
method, intrinsic - and `Function` is deleted.  A function is a value
reached by the same walk as a constant; a third namespace would let one
spelling bind a function and a constant at once, which no rule of the
language allows.

Nothing ever asked in `Function`, and nothing asked in `Value`: both
callers of `resolve_path` pass `Namespace::Type`
(`git grep -n 'Namespace::' -- compiler/src | grep -v namespace_kind`
→ 3 lines: `resolver.cryo:608`, `name_resolution.cryo:627`, and the
word inside W0011's help text), so the fold changes no answer and no
object.  The row's check moves 3 → 2.

#### D9: `where` on `type struct` / `union` / `class` / `enum`

The parser reads `parse_trait_bounds` between the head and the body
`{`; the four declaration nodes carry `where_bounds: TraitBound[]` with
`add_where_bound`; the cloner copies them; the name layer stamps them
with `stamp_trait_bounds(&node.where_bounds)` right after
`declare_generics`, so a bound's trait resolves in the declaring scope
like a method's does.  `TraitChecker::unsatisfied_trait_ref` walks a
bound list under a substitution and hands back the first bound whose
concrete argument does not implement its trait, or null; a bound whose
argument is still abstract is deferred to the concrete instantiation.

Two doors read it, because an instantiation reaches the compiler by two
routes:

* **A written annotation** - `TypeResolver::resolve_generic`, E0306
  `at(span)` of the annotation, `also_at(bound.span)`.  This is the one
  with a span, and it is why `cryo check` refuses `Holder<Plain>`.
* **An instantiation only inference writes** - a struct literal, a
  static call, a clone's concretized argument - reaches the
  monomorphizer's `refuse_unsatisfied_type_bounds` with the template and
  its arguments in hand; E0306 at the bound, naming the instantiation.
  It does not bump `error_count` itself: doing so produced a spurious
  E0900 on top of the real report.

`docs/cryo.md` §11.3 carries the rule and an example; `docs/grammar.md`
adds `("where" WhereClause)?` to the four aggregate productions.

Tests: `tests/tests/lang/type_where_bound.cryo` (2, a struct and an
enum instantiated under a satisfied bound); negatives
`E0306_type_where_bound` and `E0306_enum_where_bound` (the annotation
door, under `cryo check`); project `type_where_bound_inferred`
(`compile_fail`, the mono door: `Holder::wrap(Plain{..})` with no
annotation naming `Holder<Plain>` → E0306 at `src/main.cryo:7:32`; its
inversion, `implement trait Tagged for struct Plain` added, compiles and
returns 7).  Name resolution is fatal per module, so the two doors need
two programs, and `cryo check` stops before mono, so the mono door needs
a PROJECT rather than a negative file.

Outside the ledger: 10 files, +242 / -17, plus 6 new test files (+155).

#### Gates

`check-fast` OK; `test-census` `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail:
191 passed; projects: 55 passed)`, roster 2,122 / 191 / 58
(`.objcmp/m18-census.log`); `lsp-check` OK, 264 modules
(`.objcmp/m16-lsp.log`); `cross-check` OK (`.objcmp/m16-cross.log`);
objects (`.objcmp/m17-objcmp.out`, with `type_where_bound.cryo` moved
out because HEAD's parser refuses `where` on a struct and cannot build
that half): **examples 0 of 1,126, tests 0 of 2,332** - a pure fold and

### 8.214 D23, seventh door: `head_type_key`'s 442 were a keyword primitive with no slot, not an unstamped head - and a primitive `Item` was misread as symbolic - 2026-09-16

#### The characterisation

§8.211 left `head_type_key` (type resolution's synthesis-time filter
for a projection-bounded trait default, `default_method_applies_to_impl`)
entered 442 times on green programs, the arm uncharacterised.  Its
instrument printed only "entered"; this one printed the slot's state,
the annotation's variant, its spelling, the impl head and the default's
name (`corpus2.sh h1`, 7,862 lines, 0 failing halves,
`.objcmp/h1-lines.txt`), over every empty answer the function gave:

| slot | annotation | entries | what |
|---|---|---:|---|
| `Pending` | `Primitive` | **448** | `Chars`'s `Iterator<u32>` 436 (stdlib, 2 per compilation), five test and example iterators with `Item = i32` 12 - `min`/`max` every time |
| `Pending` | `Named` | **0** | no unstamped nominal head anywhere |
| `Answered(GenericParam)` | `Named` / `Pointer` | 6,978 | `Iterator<T>`, `Iterator<T*>` - a parameter, no key by design |
| `Answered(TypeRelative)` | `Named` | 436 | `FilterIter`'s `Iterator<I::Item>`, a projection written as a path - no key by design |

The outer arm was never an unstamped head.  A primitive written by its
keyword parses as `TypeAnnotation::Primitive`, which carries no `res`
slot at all - the keyword-ness D18 rules away - and `head_named_slot`
turned that into `Pending`.  The 442 → 448 is the corpus growing by
§8.213's tests.

#### The defect underneath

An empty key meant "symbolic, keep the default".  So an impl with
`Item = u32` kept every projection-bounded default whatever `u32`
implements, and a default bounded on a trait `u32` lacks was synthesized
and type-checked against it.  Control, under HEAD: a trait `Source` with
`total(&this) where This::Item: Zap { this.get().zap() }`, implemented
`Source<u32> for Nums` with no `Zap` for `u32`, and `main` calling only
`get()` - **refused**, E0358 `no method named zap found on type u32`
inside the trait's own default body; the same program with a declared
`Item` (`Num`) lacking `Zap` compiles and prints 3.  Sema's call-side
twin `ann_head_key` had the same arm, so `n.total()` was not refused at
the call either (`cryo check` exit 0) and would have failed in codegen.

#### The change

`head_type_key` matches the annotation the way its twin does: a `Named`
head goes through `n.res.require("type_resolution:annotation head")`
(the door), a `Primitive` answers its own name - the key it is
registered under, and the answer a `PrimTy` stamp gives, so D18 changes
nothing here - `Generic`/`Reference`/`Pointer` peel, and everything else
(array, tuple, function, projection) is empty by design.  `ann_head_key`
gains the same `Primitive` arm.  `head_named_slot` keeps its one other
caller, the trait-impl head's door.

Tests: `tests/tests/lang/trait_default_primitive_item.cryo` (2: the
control above compiles and `get()` answers 3; a declared `Item` with the
bound reaches the default); negative `E0358_primitive_item_default`
(`n.total()` refused at the call).  Mutation, for the twin: with
`ann_head_key`'s `Primitive` arm reverted and the type-resolution fix in
place, `cryo check` on the negative exits **0** - the arm is what
refuses the call; restored, E0358 at `31:7`.  The standing control for
the other direction is `min_max_non_monotonic` (`FixedI32`,
`Iterator<i32>`, `.min()` answers 1): `i32` implements `Ord`, so the
default is still synthesized for a primitive that satisfies the bound.

Outside the ledger: 2 compiler files, +26 / -12; 2 new test files,
roster +2 unit +1 negative.

`check-fast` OK; `test-census` `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail:
192 passed; projects: 55 passed)`, roster 2,124 / 192 / 58
(`.objcmp/u2-census.log`); `lsp-check` OK, 264 modules
(`.objcmp/u2-lsp.log`); `cross-check` OK (`.objcmp/u2-cross.log`);
objects (`.objcmp/u2-objcmp.out`, the new unit test moved out because

### 8.215 The extern block's bare C name was the last first-claimant-wins registration, and a call pinned by symbol alone bound whichever declaration registered first: a live miscompile, fixed by pinning the declaration - 2026-09-16

#### The defect (audit round 10)

`type_resolution.cryo`'s extern arm registered a declaration under its
bare C name only when `lookup_func_type(fn_node.name)` was invalid -
first claimant wins - and warned W0011 on a later block whose signature
differed, with text saying "the unqualified name resolves to the first
declaration".  Sema, on the stamp, bound the declaration the call
named; but the identifier call's pin was `CalleePin::Symbol("llabs")`,
and codegen answered a symbol through `symbol_signature` - the FIRST
overload entry carrying it, with the comment "they share the signature,
so the first answers", the very premise W0011 exists to say is
violated.  So sema checked the arguments against one declaration and
codegen emitted the call at another's.

Reproducer, three files: `first.cryo` declares `llabs(i32) -> i32`,
`second.cryo` declares `llabs(i64) -> i64`, `main.cryo` imports
`Second::{ llabs }` and calls `llabs(-4294967301)`.  At HEAD
(`631fedba`): builds, `declare i32 @llabs(i32)`, the argument
truncated, **exit 3 where 7 is correct**.  Under the pin `db5af63c` the
same program is REFUSED (E0214: the old model bound the first claimant
in sema too, so the i64 argument mismatched) - a program the pin
refused had become a silent miscompile.  The second shape, both
declarations called from one module through their qualified paths with
the narrow one first, the pin **compiles and exits 4** for 7: that one
was a miscompile under the old model as well.

Corpus population: `grep -c W0011` over a stdlib build → 0; the one
test, `W0011_duplicate_extern_symbol.cryo`, never calls the symbol.
Empty by luck.

#### The fix: the pin carries the declaration

* **Sema.**  `try_pin_overload_mangled_callee` pins a family of ONE
  signature by the family (`CalleePin::Family(family)`, the
  declaration's key) and a set by the selected signature's own symbol,
  which a Cryo mangling makes unique - the qualified `Module::f()` call
  and the value form already pinned the family ("a free function's
  registry key is its qualified name"); the identifier call now agrees.
  The pin reader on re-resolution reads a family's one signature through
  `lookup_func_type(fam)` so `![implicit]` converters are inserted for
  it as for a symbol: found by the unit suite, not by reasoning -
  `ImplicitArgConversion::string_literal_converts_to_owned_string`
  crashed (0xC0000374) on the first cut, because the `Family` arm
  returned the registered return early and skipped the converter.
* **Codegen.**  A free or extern call is emitted at the PINNED
  signature's function type (`pinned_signature` → `build_function_ltype`),
  not at `LLVMGlobalGetValueType` of the symbol - which is declared once
  per LLVM module, at whichever declaration reached it first.  With
  opaque pointers `call i64 @llabs(i64 %x)` against
  `declare i32 @llabs(i32)` is well-formed IR, and it is what Rust
  emits for the same program (`clashing_extern_declarations` is a
  warn-by-default lint there, and each call uses its own item's
  signature).  A method's symbol is its own mangling, so a method call
  keeps the declared type.
* **Type resolution.**  The extern declaration is registered under its
  own key (`decl_fn_key`) and nothing else; the bare-name claim, the
  `ext_bare_taken` guard, `extern_bare_owner` and its two accessors are
  deleted - with the comment that a bare `malloc` "has to bind to the
  compiler-backed intrinsic", a rule D19 made an error.  W0011 is keyed
  by the SYMBOL (`extern_symbol_first`: the first extern block's key and
  function type under each C name; an intrinsic reaching the same C
  name is not an extern block and stays silent, as before - the first
  cut compared every entry under the symbol and warned on
  `libc::malloc`/`realloc`/`free` against `intrinsics::` in every build)
  and its text says what is true now: a call binds the declaration it
  names, and at most one of the two matches the C definition.
* **Codegen's `strcmp`.**  The one reader of the bare extern key over
  the six halves was string equality's `resolve_function("strcmp")`
  (`expr_ops.cryo`), which already declared its own fallback when the
  index had none.  It declares its runtime dependency once per LLVM
  module and asks the index nothing.

#### Measurement before the deletion

Every name-keyed index reader probed against the extern-claimed keys
(`extern_bare_owner_of(name) != 0`), `corpus2.sh x1`,
`.objcmp/x1-lines.txt`, six halves:

| reader | hits | what |
|---|---:|---|
| `lookup_func_type_overloads` + `lookup_overload_mangled` | 1,007 + 1,007 | ONE key per half (`strcmp`: 993 pairs in the LSP, 14 in the unit suite, whose `string_as_cstr.cryo` also declares it) - `resolve_function("strcmp")` |
| `lookup_func_type` | 12 | the registration's own `ext_bare_taken` / `prev_type` reads, on a second declaration of one name |
| `lookup_func_return`, `lookup_mangled_name`, `get_function_module` | 0 | |

#### Mutation proof, both directions

`tests/tests/projects/extern_duplicate_symbol_binds_declaration` (run,
exit 7) and `extern_duplicate_symbol_both_called` (run, exit 7) are the
population.  Old path: HEAD's compiler exits 3 on the first; the pin
exits 4 on the second (objcmp's HEAD half also builds both, and reports
them failing there).  New path: 7 and 7, IR `call i64 @llabs(i64 %load)`
beside `declare i32 @llabs(i32)`.  The narrow declaration's own call in
the second project answers -5, as C does for a caller that passes 32
bits where the callee reads 64: the program wrote the wrong signature,
and the test asserts only the declaration the wide call named.

Outside the ledger: 5 compiler files, 2 new projects (6 files), the
lane golden.

#### Gates

`check-fast` OK; `test-census` `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail:
192 passed; projects: 57 passed)`, roster 2,124 / 192 / 60
(`.objcmp/u3-census.log`); `lsp-check` OK, 264 modules, 0 W0011
(`.objcmp/u3-lsp.log`); `cross-check` OK (`.objcmp/u3-cross.log`);
objects (`.objcmp/u3-objcmp.out`): **examples 0 of 1,126, tests 4 of
2,446 - the two new projects' `Main.o`, once per side**, HEAD's half

### 8.216 The callee pin carries a declaration: the index's function registry gets one entry per definition (a symbol is part of its identity), registration returns the entry and stamps the node, and every consumer that mangled a symbol to name a declaration reads the entry instead - 2026-09-16

#### What the pin was

`CalleePin::Symbol(s)` carried the linker symbol as a string, and every
reader of it asked the index by that string: codegen's `resolve_symbol`
through `mangled_to_overload_pos`, `pinned_signature` through
`symbol_signature`, sema's re-resolution reader through
`lookup_func_type_by_mangled` - each taking the FIRST entry under the
symbol.  Every writer of it computed the string: sema's
`pin_method_callee_from_qname` and codegen's `declare_method`,
`codegen_method_prologue` and the vtable slot each ran
`MangledName::for_method_or_trait_impl` + `with_method_spec_args` "in
lockstep" with `register_methods_with_module`; `lambda_synth` and
`free_function_symbol` ran `for_free_function`; mono's
`mangled_symbol_for_spec_method` ran the method mangling once more.
Seven copies of one computation, each a place the symbol could come
apart from the registration's.  The symbol readers were 16 sites over
four index accessors (`lookup_mangled_name` 9, `lookup_overload_mangled`
5, `symbol_signature` 1, `lookup_func_type_by_mangled` 1); the writers
15 `set_resolved_callee(CalleePin::Symbol(...))` and the vtable slot's
`resolve_pinned(CalleePin::Symbol(computed))`.

#### Measurement before the change (`corpus2.sh p1`, `.objcmp/p1-lines.txt`, 2,660,779 lines, 0 failing halves)

| what | population |
|---|---:|
| symbol reads (`lookup_func_type_by_mangled`, `symbol_signature`) naming exactly ONE entry | 1,239,625 + 54,348 |
| symbol reads naming several entries | **0** |
| symbol reads naming no entry (a mint the index never registered) | 500 + 24 |
| codegen `resolve_symbol`: held by the module / declared extern from its one entry / held with no entry | 459,296 / 29,493 / 12 |
| sema pin writes whose `(key, signature)` had exactly one entry | 130,894 of 130,894 |
| `family_overload_symbol`'s `lookup_mangled_name` fallback rung entered | **0** of 42,577 |
| `family_answer` plural | 0 |
| an entry RESTAMPED with a second symbol (`register_overload_mangled` on an entry already carrying a different one) | **11,493**, over 229 keys |
| codegen method definitions whose mint had an entry | 147,434 of 147,434 |
| vtable slots with a node and an entry | 665 of 665 |

The restamps are the finding.  The registry's entry was `(key,
signature, owner)`, and three shapes put two DEFINITIONS in one entry:
an inherent method and a trait impl's of the same name and signature on
one type (`GnIf::go` inherent then `Beta::go`), two traits' same-named
methods on one type (`Display::fmt` and `Debug::fmt` on `P`), and two
specializations of one generic method whose signature does not mention
its parameter (`GroupTag::group<T>`, 12).  Each later registration
overwrote the entry's symbol, and `mangled_to_overload_pos` mapped both
symbols to the one position - so a symbol still answered its own
signature (the two share it), but `lookup_overload_mangled(key, ft)`
answered whichever registered LAST.  Every static pin
(`pin_scope_callee_combined`, `try_pin_static_method_overload`,
`pin_scope_value_static_method`) asked exactly that: over the corpus
none reached a collapsed key (0 of 88,317 `(key, ft)` reads had two
entries, because the entry WAS collapsed - the instrument could not
see it; the restamp count is the one that could).  So the symbol was
the finest identity the index held, finer than its own entry; a pin
carrying `(DefId, signature)` would have been COARSER than the string
it replaced, and collapsed `Display::fmt` onto `Debug::fmt`.

The 524 no-entry reads and the 12 held-with-no-entry: closure
specializations (`lambda_synth` minted the symbol and registered
nothing; codegen's `free_function_symbol` minted it again and
registered it itself, `DE-FREE-SLOT` 24) and four sema method pins on
iterator-adapter combinators (`take`/`filter` on a user struct) whose
template node the index never registers; mono re-pins those at
materialization.  `MONO-REG no-entry` 456 were the EMPTY symbol
(`mangled_symbol_for_spec_method` with no receiver key: no pin, and no
registration).

#### The change

* **Registry identity is `(key, signature, owner, symbol)`.**
  `register_signature` finds that entry or appends one; a registration
  carrying a symbol the entry does not already hold is a different
  definition and gets its own.  An entry also records the TRAIT its
  declaration implements (`overload_func_trait`, empty for an inherent
  method or a free function; `entry_trait` reads it) - the one property
  that tells an inherent method from a trait's under one key and one
  signature without reading the `$tr$` off the symbol.  `register_function_type`,
  `register_function_type_owned`, `register_overload_mangled`,
  `register_overload_mangled_owned`, `register_function_with_module`,
  `register_mangled_name`, `lookup_mangled_name`, `lookup_overload_mangled`,
  `symbol_signature`, `lookup_func_type_by_mangled`, the `mangled_names`
  single-slot map and the `mangled_to_overload_pos` multimap are deleted.
  `register_function_type_with_module` takes the symbol when the caller
  has one (an `extern "C"` name, a C import alias's, an intrinsic's bare
  name - which used to be registered under the Cryo mangling and then
  restamped) and mangles the signature otherwise.
* **`OverloadId`** (`resolver/res.cryo`, beside `DefId`): an entry
  position, minted by registration alone; `entry_symbol`,
  `entry_signature`, `entry_key`, `lookup_family_entries(key)`,
  `lookup_sole_entry(key)` read it.  The two `lookup_*` are the only
  name-keyed readers added and are named so the lane gate counts them.
* **The node carries its entry.**  `FunctionDeclNode.overload_entry`,
  written by `register_methods_with_module`, the free-function arm, the
  extern arm and `lambda_synth`'s registration of the closure
  specialization (which now registers, as any declaration).  A clone
  starts unstamped.
* **`CalleePin::Symbol(SymbolStr)` → `CalleePin::Decl(OverloadId)`.**
  Writers: sema's identifier call pins the entry its arguments selected
  (the one-signature family no longer needs the `Family` form §8.215 gave
  it); `pin_method_callee_from_qname` pins the bound node's entry and
  mangles nothing (the `![symbol]` arm folds in: the entry's symbol IS the
  link name); the three static pins select among `lookup_family_entries`
  and pin the entry (`choose_entry`: one fit is it; an inherent method
  beside trait methods of the fitting signature is it, as a `Type::method`
  path names the inherent item in Rust; several trait methods and no
  inherent one is a tie that pins nothing); mono pins `spec_method.func.overload_entry` after
  registering it, and `MonoState` records the entry beside the
  materialization key so a later call to the same spec pins the same
  entry; `lambda_synth` pins the entry it registered; the vtable slot pins
  the slot method's node's entry.  Readers: `resolve_decl(e)` (held under
  the entry's symbol, else declared extern at the entry's signature),
  `pinned_signature`, sema's re-resolution reader, `callee_is_intrinsic`
  (the entry's symbol is the leaf, or its key the intrinsic's).
* **Every codegen mint is gone.**  `declare_method`,
  `codegen_method_prologue` and `free_function_symbol` read the node's
  entry; the vtable slot's `for_method` mint, `free_function_symbol`'s
  mint-and-register fallback, `pin_method_callee_from_qname`'s and
  `lambda_synth`'s mints are deleted; `test_main_codegen` reads the test
  function's node entry and `lookup_sole_entry` for the three runtime
  entry points.  `mangled_symbol_for_spec_method` survives as mono's
  materialization DEDUP key only, no longer a pin.

#### Shadow (`corpus2.sh u1`, `.objcmp/u1-lines.txt`)

Every former mint ran beside the entry it replaced and compared symbols:
**882,763 agree, 0 disagree, 4 no-stamp** (the four combinator pins
above: the old pin named a symbol with no entry; the new writes no pin,
and mono's materialization pins the spec - `mono-lazy` 20 agree).  By
site: method-pin 544,267, method-decl 147,671, method-body 147,598,
free-def 39,441, mono-seen 1,442, mono-generic 1,135, vtable 665,
mono-lazy-existing 44, lambda 12, mono-static 7.  Failing halves 0;
`make test` `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail: 192 passed; projects:
57 passed)`.

The first cut disagreed ONCE and the unit suite failed to link on it:
`TakeIter<Counter>::fold`, a generic method spec on a receiver not yet
materialized (`recv_qname` invalid), which `register_spec_method_in_di`
registers under the TEMPLATE impl's key (`impl_node.target_key`) - an
entry whose symbol `C$tr$...TakeIter-4fold...` nothing defines.  The old
code never pinned it (`spec_sym` empty because `pin_target` was); the new
pinned the junk entry.  `pin_spec_entry` keeps the old rule - a spec on
a keyless receiver is not pinned - and the registration itself is a
FINDING: an entry with no definition, reachable by `lookup_family_entries`
of the template key.

#### Gates

lane-check `LOOKUP_OTHER` 41 → 30, re-pinned (`declaration_emitter` 3 →
0, `symbol_resolver` 2 → 1, `test_main_codegen` 4 → 3, `type_resolution`
1 → 0, `call_resolver` 23 → 18).  cross-check OK (`.objcmp/u1-cross.log`).
lsp-check OK (264 modules, 0 errors); `make test-census` OK, 2,124 /
192 / 61 (the run project below, roster `--merge`).

**Objects: 3 of 2,446 + 1,126 moved** (`hash-tree.sh B` and `C` against
HEAD's half `A`, `.objcmp/u1-hashB.out`, `u1-hashC.out`; the 54 objects
of the new project are present in `C` alone and are not movers):
`Lambdas.o`, `MoveLambda.o` and `examples/13-closures/Main.o`, every one

(`.objcmp/ir-head`, `ir-tree`): 2 of 366 unit `.ll` files differ, 48 + 8
lines, and every changed line is a `__cl_NNNN` symbol renamed -
`apply__cl_7134` → `7135`, `7137` → `7139`, `7140` → `7143`, `7143` →
`7147` (0 changed lines without `__cl_`), definition and call site

#### What this leaves

* `CalleePin::Family` stays for the pins written before an entry

* **A `Type::method` path over two entries of one signature.**  Probes

  | probe | HEAD | tree before `choose_entry` | tree |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `plural_static` | 33 | E0636 `codegen: cannot resolve 'P::go'` | **33** |
  | `plural_method` | 3 | 3 | 3 |
  | `plural_trait` | 5 (`Gamma`, registered last) | E0636 | E0636 |
  HEAD's 33 came from `lookup_overload_mangled(P::go, ft)` over the

#### Rulings logged (Jake, 2026-09-16; all three RULED - UNBUILT, none built here)

* **D24 - re-key the trait-impl registry by the trait's identity.**  "I
  want to rekey."  The measurement stands as §8.212 recorded it: 1
  registration collapse and 3 wrong-block bound checks of 84,514, all in
  `trait_leaf_dispatch`.  The previous re-key was backed out for being
  decided rather than measured; that objection is discharged.  §0's D24
  row flips from MEASURED-awaiting-Jake to RULED - UNBUILT.
* **D18, the alias half - option (b): `int` folds to `PrimTy("i32")` at
  the name layer.**  A LANGUAGE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, not a requalification:
  `implement trait Show for int` is dead today (registered under the
  spelling "int", which no receiver key asks; `this` unbound, E0201;
  both receivers E0358) and becomes live and reachable from an `i32`
  receiver.  It lines up with the keyword ruling (§8.165): a primitive
  name resolves only after every scope fails to bind it, and `int` is a
  prelude alias with no identity of its own.  `HANDOFF.md` §4.1 holds the
  scoping (the third alias-table copy to avoid; who still reads
  `lookup_type_exact("int")` once every written alias is folded).
* **§9 Q2 - an `extern module` alias gets a real module-graph entry with
  a stamp.**  "I don't want to have that permanent blemish": the alias is
  not left a bare namespace symbol that resolution special-cases forever.
  `extern module libc as cit;` is already a declaration in source and
  simply is not registered, so stamping it registers what the programmer
  wrote rather than inventing a synthetic module; Rust binds `extern
  crate foo as bar` as a real nameable item.  It unblocks codegen's
  `resolve_global` lane (`resolve_global` / `_in_namespace` /
  `_by_qualified`, 5 call sites) and its five-step spelling ladder, which
  exists because the alias has no stamp, and `lookup_callee_function_type`'s
  `bare_sym` door.  Scoping owed before it is built, not gating: which of
  those sites resolve the ALIAS itself and which a MEMBER inside the
  `cit::X` wholesale key space - stamping the alias plausibly closes the
  first and leaves the second as a separate, smaller question.  New §0 row
  `Q2`, beside D24.

### 8.217 The scope-call argument check keys a module segment by its stamp; the module-suffix scan behind the spelling is deleted - at a tied suffix it checked nothing, and a mismatched argument compiled into a binary that died of heap corruption - 2026-09-16

#### What the scan was

`check_scope_call_arg_types` (`sema/call_resolver.cryo`) type-checks the
arguments of a `Scope::member(args)` call against the one signature
registered under the callee's key, and is the ONLY place a module-qualified
call's arguments are checked (measured below).  It keyed the call by
`<spelling>::<member>`, where the spelling came from `scope_owner_key`,
which answers `scope.scope_name` for a `Res::Def` segment - a module
qualifier is not a type-owner claim, so that function leaves it as written.
`fmt::println` is not the key `std::fmt::println` is registered under, so
every abbreviated module call missed the exact key and fell into a second
lane: walk every module in the graph, match the written scope as a
whole-segment suffix of each namespace, and take the one candidate whose
`<namespace>::<member>` has exactly one overload.  Its comment still
explained itself by mirroring `resolve_module_qualified_function`'s
suffix match - a lane M5 deleted (§0 L122); the stamp has named the module
since.

#### Shadow (`corpus2.sh u2`, `.objcmp/u2-lines.txt`, 162,460 lines, 0 failing halves, `make test` OVERALL PASS 58 projects)

At the scan, the stamp's answer was computed beside it -
`resolve_module_qualified_symbol(scope_name, member_name, scope)`, the one
path that resolves a module call's RETURN - and the two compared:

| shape | lines |
|---|---:|
| module segment, scan named one function, the stamp the same one | 126,642 |
| type segment: no exact overloads, the scan walked every module, found nothing | 35,804 |
| **module segment, the scan named nothing, the stamp answers** | **14** |

The 14 (`.objcmp/u1-keep/u2-disagree.txt`), every one a `Def` segment:
12 where two modules share the written suffix - `resolution_module_suffix`
`Code::val` (2) and `Text::tag` (2), `resolution_trait_default` `Text::tag`
under `Alpha` (4) and `Beta` (4) - so the scan found two candidates, tied,
and CHECKED NOTHING; 2 a re-export, `reexport_basic` writing
`Aggregate::make_widget` for what the stamp names
`ReexportBasic::Inner::make_widget`, which no namespace's suffix reaches.
The scan was never right where the stamp was wrong.

#### The check it skipped is the only one

Every `check_args_against_params` caller was tagged with the call's
position and a probe built under HEAD `1451d792` and the tree
(`.objcmp/u1-keep/u2mut/`: `Alpha::Text::tag() -> i32` and
`Beta::Text::tag(s: String) -> i32`, both in the graph through a registry
module, `main` importing `Beta::Text`):

| `Text::tag(...)` | HEAD `1451d792` | tree |
|---|---|---|
| `("hello")` | builds; the binary exits `0xC0000374` STATUS_HEAP_CORRUPTION | builds; exits **5** |
| `(5)` against `String` | **builds**, no diagnostic; `0xC0000374` | **E0214** `expected String, found i32` |
| `("a", "b")` | E0900 `LLVM module verification failed: Incorrect number of arguments` | **E0215** `takes 1 argument(s) but 2 were supplied` |

Under HEAD no `check_args_against_params` caller reached the call at all
(0 tagged lines at its position, `head-*.log`): at a tied suffix the
module call's arguments were checked by NOTHING, the raw literal or the
`i32` was passed where a by-value `String` was expected, and the callee's
drop freed garbage.  Under the tree the module arm reaches it (`tree-*.log`,
`scope-arm` 2-3 lines at `7:24`) and nothing else does - so the arm is
not a second copy of a check the family reader also performs (the
identifier call's converter path is for identifier calls, and the earlier
probe that suggested otherwise was measuring a graph with ONE `::Text`
module: `alpha_text.cryo` was imported by nothing and never compiled).

#### The change

`check_scope_call_arg_types` dispatches on the segment's stamp as
`resolve_scope_call` does: a `Def` segment's key is
`resolve_module_qualified_symbol`'s answer (the stamp's qualified name +
member, gated on a registered return), a type segment's the owner key as
before.  The suffix scan, its M5 comment, and the dead
`import compiler::module_graph::{ ModuleInfo }` are deleted; a module
segment with no such key, or several overloads, returns instead of
falling into the inherent static-method gather (a module owns no static
methods; the name layer refuses a module and a type sharing one name).
`require_scope_res` 14 → 15, `names_module` 3 → 7.

Two run projects hold the pair: `module_suffix_tie_checks_arguments`
(the conversion, exit 5; HEAD's binary crashes) and
`module_suffix_tie_rejects_mismatch` (`compile_fail`, E0214 with `found i32` in its label; HEAD compiles it).

#### Gates

lsp-check OK (264 modules, 0 errors); cross-check OK (`.objcmp/u2-cross.log`);
`make test-census` OK, 2,124 / 192 / 63 (roster `--merge`, +2);
lane-check `LOOKUP_OTHER` 30 → 28 (`call_resolver` 18 → 16, the scan's
two `lookup_func_type_overloads` reads), re-pinned; ns-status-check OK
(232 rows).  **Objects: 0 of 2,500 + 1,126 moved** (`hash-tree.sh D`
against `C`, HEAD `838f4478`'s half, `.objcmp/u2-hashD.out`: examples 0,
tests 57 = the two new projects' objects present in `D` alone,
2,557 − 2,500).  The 14 sites' calls compile to the same objects: their
arguments already fit, and the conversion the scan skipped was not needed
at any of them - the corpus was empty of the crash by luck, which is what
the two projects are for.

#### What this leaves

* `scope_owner_key` still answers a `Def` segment's SPELLING to its four
  other callers (`:302`, `:3580`, `:3881`, `:3928`), each a type-owner
  context where a module segment should name nothing; unmeasured.
* The `E0900` an arity-wrong call produced under HEAD is LLVM's verifier
  catching what sema did not - a codegen-layer refusal of a sema error,
  the same shape as §8.216's E0636.

Outside the ledger: `sema/call_resolver.cryo`, two projects, the roster
and lane goldens.

**Tally: 70 shadowed, 70 old paths deleted, 70 at zero; 105 artifacts
gone** (+ the module-suffix scan).

### 8.218 The index's per-module ownership tables are deleted: written on every registration, read by nothing - 2026-09-16

#### What they were

`DeclarationIndex` kept, beside every function and type registration, the
module that registered it: `module_funcs: Pair<name, module>[]`,
`module_types: Pair<name, module>[]`, and two O(1) indices over the first
- `module_func_first` (name → first module, "first-wins ownership") and
`module_func_pairs` (a packed `(name, module)` membership set) - written
by `note_module_func` on every push.  Four accessors read them:
`get_functions_in_module`, `is_function_in_module`,
`get_function_module`, `get_type_module`; the header comment said codegen
used them to enumerate a module's exports for the define-vs-extern
decision.  Three registrars took a `module` argument to feed them -
`register_methods_with_module` (12 callers), `register_function_type_with_module`
(5), `register_type_with_module` (9) - and `owner_mod` was plumbed from
`SpecInjector::register` through `register_injected_decl` into
`register_decl_in_index` so that an injected specialization's ownership
would name its template's module rather than the demanding one.

#### Measurement (the current tree at `ccb310aa`, `grep -rl <name> compiler/src tools --include=*.cryo`)

| symbol | files outside `decl_index.cryo` |
|---|---|
| `module_func_first`, `module_func_pairs`, `note_module_func` | 0 |
| `module_types` | 1 - a comment, `type_resolution.cryo:453` |
| `get_type_module` | 1 - `arena.cryo`, the arena's own method of that name |
| `get_function_module`, `is_function_in_module`, `get_functions_in_module` | 0 |
| `module_funcs` | 1 - `sema/diagnostics.cryo` `collect_bare_callable_names`, reading `.first` |

Inside the file the four accessors were the only readers of the four
tables (`module_func_pairs` also gated the `module_funcs` push against a
second overload of one method).  `module_funcs.second` was read by
`get_functions_in_module` alone.  So every table was write-only through
its accessors, and the one outside reader wanted the function NAMES.
ABSENT, not starved: nothing asked; a clean deletion, no shadow to run.

Control on the instrument: the grep that reports 0 for the accessors
finds the arena's `get_type_module` and the comment mentioning
`module_types`, so it is not a grep that finds nothing.

#### The change

* The four tables, `note_module_func` and the four accessors are
  deleted.  `module_funcs` becomes `callable_names: u32[]` - every
  function key ever registered, once, in registration order, deduplicated
  at the push by `callable_names_seen` - and `collect_bare_callable_names`
  reads it; its own string dedup goes, since interned symbols make id
  identity string identity, and its order is the old first-occurrence
  order.
* The `module` parameter comes off the registrars, which are renamed
  for what they now do: `register_methods` (the combined `Type::method`
  keys), `register_function_signature` (a free function's key, symbol
  and entry); `register_type_with_module` was `register_type` plus a
  `module_types` push and its 9 callers call `register_type`.
* `owner_mod` is stripped from `SpecInjector::register`,
  `register_injected_decl` and `register_decl_in_index`, with the
  `module_sym` locals that carried it: `type_resolution.cryo`'s
  `register_decl_in_index` head, the extern arm's `ext_mod_sym`, the
  intrinsic arm's `i_mod_sym`, `specialization.cryo`'s `register`, and
  `AsyncDecl.module_sym` in `async_lower.cryo`, a field whose only reader
  was the argument to the deleted parameter (found by the LSP gate's
  warning count moving 490 → 491, W0001 unused variable; 490 again).
  `owner_module_sym` in `specialization.cryo` stays: it also sets
  `entry.owner_source`.

#### Gates

lsp-check OK (264 modules, 0 errors, 490 warnings); cross-check OK
(`.objcmp/u3-cross2.log`); `make test-census` OK, 2,124 / 192 / 63;
lane-check unchanged (`LOOKUP_OTHER` 28: none of the deleted names was a
`lookup_*`); ns-status-check OK.  **Objects: 0 of 2,557 + 1,126 moved**
(`hash-tree.sh E` against `D`, HEAD `ccb310aa`'s half, `.objcmp/u3-hashE.out`;
`t-E.txt.log` OVERALL PASS 2,124 / 192 / 60, 0 allocation failures).

#### Findings, not chased

* `collect_bare_callable_names` keeps only keys with no `::`, and
  `decl_fn_key` qualifies every function a namespaced file declares, so
  the E0202 did-you-mean has an EMPTY population in practice: a probe with
  `helper_value()` declared and `helper_valu()` called in one file gets
  `E0202` and no suggestion, under HEAD and the tree alike
  (`.objcmp/u1-keep/dym/`).  The list is a second copy of the registry's
  keys (`overload_func_keys`) filtered to nothing; the suggestion wants
  the registry's LEAVES.
* The globals' analogue - `register_global_with_module`,
  `module_global_modules`, `get_global_module` - has ONE outside reader;
  not measured further here.

Outside the ledger: `decl_index.cryo`, `sema/diagnostics.cryo`,
`sema/async_lower.cryo`, `sema/lambda_synth.cryo`,
`mono/call_specializer.cryo`, `passes/specialization.cryo`,
`passes/type_resolution.cryo`.

**Tally: 70 shadowed, 70 old paths deleted, 70 at zero; 114 artifacts
gone** (+ four tables, four accessors, `note_module_func`, a field, and
the `module`/`owner_mod` parameter of six functions - counted as nine:
the tables and accessors, and the parameter chain as one).

### 8.219 A stamped declaration answers its type through the index by its id: `type_of_def` / `func_type_of_def`, and six readers that unwrapped a `DefId` to key a lookup hand the id over instead - 2026-09-16

#### The shape

A `Res::Def(q)` is the name layer's answer, and `q` is a `DefId`.  Six
readers held one and turned it back into a string to ask the index the
type it names - `q.qualified_name()` then `lookup_type` (the index
directly, 2) or `lookup_type_exact` / `lookup_func_type_exact` (through
`TypeUtils`, 4).  Each is a `DEFID_UNWRAP` whose only consumer is a
name-keyed lookup, which is the case the lane baseline's own header calls
out: "a re-keyed lookup here has re-derived what it was handed, and
should take the DefId instead".  The index already answered a `Res`
without a caller-side unwrap (`type_of_res`, `func_type_of_res`, each
unwrapping once inside the index); a `DefId` in hand had no such door.

#### The change

* `DeclarationIndex::type_of_def(DefId)` and `func_type_of_def(DefId)`:
  the definition's canonical name is the map's key, so the id is
  unwrapped there and nowhere a reader stands.  `type_of_res` and
  `func_type_of_res` ride on them (the index's `DEFID_UNWRAP` stays 2).
* Six sites hand the id over: `TypeResolutionPasses::impl_owner`'s `Def`
  arm; the class base (`require_base_res` → `type_of_res`, its local
  `base_q` gone); `pattern_resolver`'s enum pattern type; the struct
  literal's base in `sema`; `TypeUtils::def_type`, the DefId-keyed door
  that records an unregistered definition, which unwrapped internally;
  and the function VALUE's type in `sema` (`func_type_of_res`).  At the
  last, the canonical name is still derived once, for the `Family` pin
  and the visibility gate - both keyed by name by design - so that
  unwrap stays and the entry says why.
* Not taken, each unwrap being for TEXT or for a name-keyed consumer of
  another kind: the base-constructor symbol (`decl_visit_emitter`), the
  `Family` pins, `callee_family`, `resolve_module_qualified_symbol`'s key
  build, the const table's qualified-name reads, the generic registry's
  `get_template(def.qualified_name())`, the annotation-head keys.  Those
  are the next slices: each wants its consumer re-keyed, not just the
  lookup.

#### Gates

lane-check `LOOKUP` 43 → 41 (`type_resolution` 21 → 19, the two
`lookup_type` calls), `DEFID_UNWRAP` 38 → 33 (`type_resolution` 5 → 3,
`pattern_resolver` 1 → 0, `sema` 2 → 1, `type_utils` 4 → 3), re-pinned;
predicted −2 and −6 before the edit, the sixth unwrap kept for the pin as
above.  lsp-check OK (490 warnings); cross-check OK (`.objcmp/u4-cross.log`);
`make test-census` OK, 2,124 / 192 / 63; ns-status-check OK (a new row).
**Objects: 0 of 2,557 + 1,126 moved** (`hash-tree.sh F` against `E`, HEAD
`41208b28`'s half, `.objcmp/u4-hashF.out`; `t-F.txt.log` OVERALL PASS
2,124 / 192 / 60, 0 allocation failures) - the same map under the same
key, asked with the id instead of the id's name.

Outside the ledger: `decl_index.cryo`, `passes/type_resolution.cryo`,
`sema/pattern_resolver.cryo`, `sema/sema.cryo`, `sema/type_utils.cryo`,
the lane golden.

**Tally: 70 shadowed, 70 old paths deleted, 70 at zero; 114 artifacts
gone** (unchanged: a requalification, nothing deleted; the lane rows

### 8.220 A `Type::method` path two traits provide at one signature is reported in sema as E0154, naming both traits; codegen's E0636 / E0900 refusal of the unpinned path was the wrong layer with the wrong text - 2026-09-16

#### The shape

§8.216's `choose_entry` selects the entry a `Type::method` path names
from the fits its signature (value form) or its arguments (call form)
leave: one fit is it, an inherent method beside trait methods is it, and
several trait methods with no inherent one is a tie that pins nothing.
Unpinned, the path reached codegen, which has no spelling fallback for a
scope call since the `mangled_names` map went, and refused it there: the
call form as E0636 `codegen: cannot resolve 'P::go'` / `no such
associated function` (the method exists twice, not never), the value
form - `pin_scope_value_static_method` falls to `CalleePin::Family` - as
E0900 "names several functions and the call was not pinned to one of
them" (true, and unexplained).  Rust reports both forms of this tie as
one error, E0034 "multiple applicable items in scope", with a note per
candidate ("candidate #1 is defined in an impl of the trait `Beta` for
the type `P`").  Cryo's method-call form of the same tie, `p.go()`, is
already E0154 (`sema/call_resolver.cryo`, "call to `go` is ambiguous: it
is provided by multiple traits implemented for this type"; §13.4 of
`docs/cryo.md` names the code).  The static-path form is the same
ambiguity spelled as a path, so it is reported under the same code, as
Rust does; a distinct code for the path spelling is Jake's to mint if he
wants one, and is a one-line change.

#### The change

`choose_entry` takes the path node and, at a tie of two or more trait
entries with no inherent one, reports it (`report_static_path_tie`):
E0154 "`P::go` is ambiguous: `go` is provided by more than one trait
implemented for `P`", the label naming both traits, a note per candidate
in Rust's words, and nothing during a symbolic generic-body walk (the
concrete instantiation reports, as the method form's guard does).  Both
callers hand the node over: `try_pin_static_method_overload` (the call
form, from `pin_scope_callee_combined`) and `entry_of_signature` (the
value form).  No pinning decision moved: every non-tie answer is the one
`choose_entry` gave before.

Probes (scratch, each under the tree's compiler before and after):
| probe | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `tie`: `Beta::go(&this)` + `Gamma::go(&this)` for `P`, `P::go(&p)` | E0636 at codegen | E0154 at sema |
| `stat_call`: `static make()` in both traits, `P::make()` | E0636 at codegen | E0154 at sema |
| `stat_value`: `const f: () -> i32 = P::make;` | E0900 at codegen | E0154 at sema |
| `disamb`: `Beta::go(&p) * 10 + Gamma::go(&p)` | E0636 at codegen | E0636 at codegen |

The last row is a **finding**: the explicit trait-path call
`Trait::method(receiver, args)`, which the method-form E0154's own note
proposes as the disambiguation ("disambiguate by calling the trait method
explicitly, e.g. `Trait::method(receiver, args)`") and §13.4 describes
("resolved by calling the trait method explicitly"), compiles under no
compiler in reach - not the tree, not HEAD `1451d792`'s
(`.objcmp/cryo-head.exe`), not the pin (`bin/cryo.exe`, 2026-09-11):
sema types it silently and codegen refuses `Beta::go` as unknown.  The
corpus holds no use of the form (`grep -rn -E
'[A-Z][A-Za-z]+::[a-z_]+\(&[a-z_]+[,)]' tests/tests examples` finds only
`Type::method(&recv)` static calls on inherent methods).  So the
diagnostic for the tie names no way out today: the language has no
working trait-qualified call.  That form is a language question
(`Trait::method(recv)` as the note promises, Rust's `<P as Beta>::go(&p)`,
or both), Jake's, and this entry does not add a help line that promises
either.  The method form's note that promises the broken form is left as
written; its wording is Jake's too.

Negative `E0154_static_path_two_traits` (2 annotations: the call form
`CfP::go(&p)` and the value form `CfP::make`).  **Mutation pair**: the
same file through `cryo check` under the pin and under `1451d792`'s
compiler exits 0 - sema alone accepts the ambiguous program, the refusal
lived only in codegen - and under the tree exits with the two E0154s.
`static_path_prefers_inherent_method` (the inherent-wins rule, exit 33)
passes unchanged.

#### Gates

`make test` (in `hash-tree.sh G`'s log, `.objcmp/t-G.txt.log`) OVERALL
PASS: unit ok, compile-fail 192 → **193**, projects 60; roster merged
(`roster-check --merge`, 1 added).  lsp-check OK (490 warnings);
cross-check OK (`.objcmp/u1-cross.log`).  **Objects: 0 of 2,557 + 1,126
moved** (`hash-tree.sh G` against `F`, HEAD `ed99b6a3`'s half,
`.objcmp/hash-G.out`; predicted 0: a diagnostic on a path no green
program reaches - §8.216 measured 0 corpus programs at the codegen
refusal, and codegen has no fallback a sema refusal could pre-empt).
lane-check unchanged (no lookup added; `LOOKUP` 41, `DEFID_UNWRAP` 33).
§0: the negative count 192 → 193.

Outside the ledger: `sema/call_resolver.cryo`, the negative, the roster.

### 8.221 `register_decl_in_index` asked the index for a written type under its own key and registered the answer back under the same key, six arms; deleted - 2026-09-16

#### The shape

Every one of the six type-declaration arms of `register_decl_in_index`
(struct, union, class, enum, trait, alias) opened with the pair

    const qualified_sym = ctx.decl_type_key(node.name, ..., node.span.file);
    const ty = ctx.decl_index.lookup_type(qualified_sym);
    if (ty.is_valid()) { ctx.decl_index.register_type(qualified_sym, ty); }

- a name-keyed lookup whose only consumer was a registration of what it
found under the key it was found by.  `register_type(k, ty)` writes
`type_map[k] = ty` and `type_reverse[ty] = k`, so the pair is a no-op
unless the reverse map named some OTHER key for that type at the time -
a repair of `lookup_type_name`'s answer that nothing said it was, and
that nothing would have noticed disappearing.  The six were 6 of the 19
`LOOKUP` sites in `type_resolution.cryo`, audit 10's bucket B (a key
derived from a declaration in hand); the type-declaration stage
(`pass_registry.cryo`) had already registered every one of these types
under exactly this key.

#### The measurement

A shadow before each re-registration (`shadow_rdi`): `agree` when the
map held the key and `lookup_type_name(ty)` was already the key,
`DISAGREE` with both names otherwise, and `INVALID` when the key was
not registered at all; tagged `src`/`clone` by `is_source_decl`.  Six
halves (`corpus2.sh u2`, `.objcmp/u2-lines.txt`): **37,976 lines, all
`agree`** - struct 20,520, trait 9,295, enum 8,020, class 132, union 6,
alias 3; **0 `clone`** (the spec injector registers a clone's type itself
under the arena name, and its fallback into these arms was never taken);
0 `DISAGREE`, 0 `INVALID`; 0 failing halves; `make test` in the run
OVERALL PASS 193 / 60.  Control by inversion: the comparison flipped
(`prev.id != key.id`), the same scratch project printed 166 `DISAGREE`
and 0 `agree` where it had printed 166 `agree` - the instrument reports a
disagreement when there is one.  ABSENT, not starved: the repair had
nothing to repair.

#### The change

The six pairs are deleted; the arms keep what the type-declaration stage
does not own - `register_name_mapping`, `set_decl_visibility`,
`register_methods` - each still keyed by `decl_type_key`, which is the
slice that wants the node to carry its registration's id (next).  The
doc comment says the arm asks the index nothing about the type.

#### Gates

lane-check `LOOKUP` 41 → **35** (`type_resolution` 19 → 13), re-pinned;
predicted −6.  **Objects: 0 of 2,557 + 1,126 moved** (`hash-tree.sh H`
against `G`, HEAD `a577364f`'s half, `.objcmp/hash-H.out`; `t-H.txt.log`
OVERALL PASS unit ok / 193 / 60); predicted 0.  lsp-check OK (490
warnings).  §0: the `LOOKUP` cell 41 → 35 on §8.219's row; a new
machinery row.

Outside the ledger: `passes/type_resolution.cryo`, the lane golden.

**Tally: 71 shadowed, 71 old paths deleted, 71 at zero; 114 artifacts
gone** (+1 lane, the re-registration pair, shadowed and deleted here; the
artifact count is unchanged - the pair was inline, and no named function
or table went with it).

### 8.222 `is_candidate_public`'s permissive default answered "public" for every extern-block function - a `private` extern was callable by qualified path from any module; every registration records its verdict now, and a candidate with none is a recorded defect - 2026-09-17

#### The shape

`DeclarationIndex::is_candidate_public(q)` read `decl_visibility` and
answered `true` for a key with no entry.  Three doors ask it:
`enforce_callee_visibility` (sema, the E0353 gate for a qualified call
and for a function taken as a value), and the two E0203 explainers in
type resolution, `unreachable_declarer` and `suggest_reaching_import`.
The default sat outside `lane-check` by construction - no `lookup_*`
name - while D12 names `lane-check` as the enforcement for exactly this
class.  Audit 9 flagged it; nothing had measured whether the default was
ever the answer.

#### The measurement

A shadow at the three doors (`visibility_recorded`, a temporary index
query; door, `recorded`|`DEFAULT`, the key on `DEFAULT` only).  Six halves
(`corpus2.sh u3`, `.objcmp/u3-lines.txt`): **102,408 asks, 29,828
answered by the default.**

| door | recorded | DEFAULT |
|---|---|---|
| `callee` (`enforce_callee_visibility`) | 72,573 | **29,825** |
| `unreach` (`unreachable_declarer`) | 5 | 2 |
| `suggest` (`suggest_reaching_import`) | 2 | 1 |

The 29,825 are 237 distinct keys, every one a function declared in an
`extern` block: `std::ffi::libc` (75 keys; `strlen` 4,511, `memcpy`
4,320, `printf` 2,412 ...), `std::sys::syscall` (83), `std::ffi::openssl`
(23), `compiler::bindgen::clang` (54), and the `ExtDup` project's two
`llabs`.  The extern-block arm of type resolution registers the signature
and the link symbol and never wrote a verdict; the free-function arm
writes `func.is_public` beside its registration.  The 3 type asks are one
key, `NamespaceGate::Depot::Crate`, a generic struct asked by the E0203
explainers while resolving `Orphan` - a module that does not import
`Depot` and so is resolved before `Depot`'s Phase 4 (where
`register_decl_in_index` wrote a type's verdict) has run; the verdict
existed later, not yet.

STARVED of a writer, not absent - and load-bearing in the wrong
direction.  The parser gives an extern-block function its written
visibility (`private function llabs(v: i64) -> i64;` is `is_public =
false`; the parser's own comment says a private one binds nothing at an
`import ... { llabs }`), and the qualified path around that: probe
`.objcmp/u1-keep/privext` - `PrivExt::Ffi` declares the private extern,
`PrivExt::Main` calls `Ffi::llabs(-9)` - **compiled and ran under HEAD
(`767e956f`), exit 9**; the shadow shows the one `DEFAULT` line for it.

#### The change

* **Every type registration records its verdict with its key.**
  `register_type(key, ty)` → `register_type(key, ty, is_public)`,
  writing `decl_visibility` in the same call, so no type is ever in the
  map without one and no reader can be earlier than the write.  28
  callers: the type-declaration stage's six (`node.is_public`; a trait
  and an alias carry no modifier and are public), its 19 primitives, the
  spec injector (`SpecInjector::node_is_public`, the template's verdict
  the cloner copied onto the node), the async wrapper struct and the
  closure struct (synthesized, public).  `register_decl_in_index`'s five
  type-arm writes go: they were a second, later writer of the same
  verdict, and the gap above was the window between the two.
* **The extern-block arm records each imported function's verdict** under
  its key and, for a C import, under the `alias::name` key too -
  `fn_node.is_public`, the same rule the free-function arm applies.
* **The `None` arm is a door**: `record_unregistered_def(...)` - the
  build ends in E0900 "canonical name(s) named no registered declaration"
  when nothing else failed it - and it answers `true` meanwhile, the
  top-level default, so a public item whose registration lost its verdict
  is reported as the registration defect it is rather than as "private".
  The comment on `decl_visibility` no longer says "permissive".

Project `extern_private_function_is_private` (compile_fail, E0353 with
the message asserted): HEAD's compiler builds and runs it (exit 9), the
tree refuses it at the call.  **Mutation pair for the door**: with the
extern arm's write commented out, the same probe fails under the tree
with `E0900: 194 canonical name(s) named no registered declaration; first
consumed at decl_index: visibility of a candidate no registration recorded
a verdict for` (the stdlib's own extern calls), where HEAD's compiler over
the same program reported nothing and ran it.  Restored, the probe is
E0353.

Not taken: `register_type_forward_only` (the four alias keywords) records
no verdict - D18's arm, and no door asked one of its keys over the
corpus; a `Type::method` static call's visibility is
`enforce_static_method_visibility`'s, a different map.

#### Gates

`make test` (in `hash-tree.sh I`'s log, `.objcmp/t-I.txt.log`) OVERALL
PASS: unit ok, compile-fail 193, projects 60 → **61**; roster merged.
lsp-check OK (490 warnings); cross-check OK (`.objcmp/u3-cross.log`).
**Objects: 0 of 2,557 + 1,126 moved** (`hash-tree.sh I` against `H`,
HEAD `767e956f`'s half, `.objcmp/hash-I.out`); predicted 0: a verdict
map feeds diagnostics only.  lane-check unchanged (35 / 28 / 20 / 9 / 2 /
6 / 0 / 22 / 33).  §0: the project count 63 → 64; a new machinery row.

Outside the ledger: `decl_index.cryo`, `passes/pass_registry.cryo`,
`passes/specialization.cryo`, `passes/type_resolution.cryo`,
`sema/async_lower.cryo`, `sema/lambda_synth.cryo`, the project, the
