### 8.238 A specialized type is registered when its entry is placed, by the monomorphizer, so the two spec-method sites register by the receiver's TYPE: 1,662 of 1,663 named at registration (§8.235's 83 `NONAME` keys and its 480 empty keys were the same ordering seen from two sides), the one unnamed receiver is an instantiation the worklist has not drained and is deferred by kind, and `register_methods_by_key` has one caller - D18's door - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

§8.235 measured the two `call_specializer` registrations
(`register_spec_method_in_di`, `_inherent`) as an ORDERING defect: a
generic method materialized on a specialized receiver was registered
under the receiver's KEY (`impl_node.target_key`, `arena.get_qualified_
name(recv_type)`) because the receiver's type was not in the index yet -
`SpecInjector::register` wrote it when `run_generic_expression_resolution`
walked the entries after the module's monomorphization.  83 keys named no
type at that moment, every one registered later; 480 more registrations
had an EMPTY key and were skipped at the site altogether.

#### Measured

The conversion with a print at both sites (`scripts/ns-migration/8.238/
shadow.patch` over `2e3e7f42`, `corpus2.sh y1`, `.objcmp/y1-lines.txt`,
**1,663** `SPO` lines - §8.235's count exactly - `failing halves: 0`,
`OVERALL PASS … projects: 64 passed`; `cut -f4,5,7,8,9,10 | sort | uniq -c`):

| verdict | rows | what they are |
|---|---:|---|
| `AGREE` - the index names the receiver, the same string the old key was | **1,182** | every row that had a key: the 1,099 §8.235 named AND its 83 `NONAME` (`NonNull<u8>`, `String<GlobalAlloc>`, `Array<i64, GlobalAlloc>`, a test's `GgTf<i32>` - 574 rows under those four keys, all named now) |
| `NAMED-nokey` - the index names the receiver, the old site had no key | **480** | all `inherent`, all `String<GlobalAlloc>`, kind `InstantiatedType`, `materialized`, `arena-noname`: the receiver is the wrapper id **between the entry's placement and the populate-time flip** - `String`'s own bodies calling `this.push<T>` / `try_push<T>` during the nested-call walk.  §8.235 read these as "an unmaterialized `InstantiatedType`"; the instantiation WAS materialized (its entry placed, `has_materialized_spec` true), only the arena slot not yet flipped, which is why `get_qualified_name` answered nothing and the site returned.  The same 480 and the 83 were one ordering seen from two sides |
| `DISAGREE` | **0** | |
| `NONAME`, `DEFERRED` | **1** | `tests/unit`, the `impl` site, `std::core::iter::TakeIter`'s template block: a generic method walked on `TakeIter<Range<i32>>` before the worklist drained it - the corpus's only receiver that is an instantiation with NO entry placed.  The old site keyed it under the template's `std::core::iter::TakeIter`, "a definition nothing emits" (`pin_spec_entry`); nothing is registered there now and 0 objects moved |

**The door fires.**  With the type registration moved back to the pass
(`SpecInjector::register` registering the type, the monomorphizer not -
HEAD's ordering under the new sites), `examples/01-hello` is refused:
`error[E0900]: 7 canonical name(s) named no registered declaration; first
consumed at mono/spec inherent method` (`.objcmp/y3-mut-hello.log`; 7 =
hello's 2 old-`NONAME` + 5 in-window rows).  Under the by-key sites the
same ordering built hello green with the 2 keyed silently (§8.235's
`x3-lines.txt`).

#### What is there now

* The monomorphizer registers the specialized TYPE at the seam where its
  identity is decided - after `resolve_specialized_ast`, before the entry
  is pushed and the nested-call walk runs:
  `decl_index.register_type(qualified_spec_sym, concrete_type, …)`, the id
  stamped on the clone (`Monomorphizer::stamp_def`, `node_is_public` moved
  in from `SpecInjector`).  The name is the one this function minted, not
  asked of the arena: the slot is still an unflipped wrapper there and
  `get_qualified_name` answers nothing (the first cut asked the arena and
  registered no type at all - every example refused, `.objcmp/y1-ex10.log`
  500 errors).  `SpecInjector::register` registers what the clone CARRIES
  (its methods, the bare-name mapping) under the type the index already
  holds; it registers no type and stamps nothing.
* `register_spec_method_in_di` / `_inherent` call
  `register_methods(recv_type, …)` (sites `mono/spec impl method`,
  `mono/spec inherent method`) behind `receiver_unmaterialized`: an
  `InstantiatedType` with no entry placed (`!state.has_materialized_spec`)

  through the node once the owner exists; every other receiver is a type

* `register_methods_by_key` has ONE caller: D18's alias-keyword door in

### 8.239 What enters name resolution, and by which route: `resolve_path` answers 2 sites and `Resolver::lookup` - the unfiltered rib walk - answers 9, measured at 3,059,355 asks; the namespace filter binds the same symbol at every site but 417, of which 11 are a class constructor called by its name (§9 Q13); `resolve_type_qualified_name_bare_from` - `resolve_path`'s `Def` projected to a string and re-wrapped - is deleted - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

§5.2 names `resolve_path(segments, ns, scope) -> Res` as THE way into name
resolution.  Audit 11 counted its callers at 2, both one-segment, both
`Namespace::Type`, and asked what the other ways in were.  Nobody had
measured them.

The routes, enumerated (`grep -rn 'this\.resolver\.[a-z_]*(' name_resolution.cryo`;
the `Resolver`'s reading API - `lookup`, `lookup_in_module`, `lookup_prelude`,
`lookup_overloads`, `resolve_path` - has no caller outside that file):

| route | sites | what it answers |
|---|---:|---|
| `resolve_path` | 2 | the base-class name (`visit(ClassDeclNode)`); `resolve_type_qualified_name_bare_from` in `resolver.cryo`, itself called twice by `type_spelling_res` - the annotation lane's bare leaf from the writer's module scope, and the C-import alias spelling - and projecting the `Res` to a qualified-name STRING its callers re-wrapped as `Res::Def` |
| `Resolver::lookup(name, current_scope)` - the rib walk with NO namespace filter, prelude last | 9 | the identifier (`bare_name_res`, a second `Res` builder beside `res_for_head`), the scope head (`record_resolution` + `stamp_module_scope`), the annotation's generic-parameter probe and its path head (kind checks), `new`, the struct literal, the enum pattern and the impl target (`record_resolution` for the LSP; the stamp comes from `type_spelling_res`), the constant pattern (kind check) |
| `lookup_in_module` | 7 | the rooted remainder: an import's target, a re-export's, the module lane's `walk_module_rooted_type`, an ambiguity check - the segment-after-head work §5.1 says is "resolved within what the previous segment named", which `resolve_path` hands to the type layer as `TypeRelative` and the module lane finishes here |
| `lookup_overloads` | 1 | the overload SET at a call (`record_overloads`) - a different question |

#### Measured

The nine `lookup` sites with a print (`scripts/ns-migration/8.239/shadow.patch`
over `7d6705ac`, `corpus2.sh z1`, `.objcmp/z1-lines.txt`, **3,059,355** `RP`
lines, `failing halves: 0`; the suite's two output-exclusion projects read
FAIL under a shadow that prints names, the known trap): the symbol the
unfiltered walk bound beside the one the namespace-filtered walk
`resolve_path` makes would bind (`cut -f4,5,7 | sort | uniq -c`):

| verdict | rows | |
|---|---:|---|
| `SAME` | **2,552,752** | one symbol either way |
| `NONE` | 506,186 | neither binds (a primitive, a builtin, a member sema resolves) |
| `UNF-ONLY` | **385** | the unfiltered walk bound a symbol the namespace refuses and the filtered walk found nothing: 276 scope heads binding a FIELD (`headers::push_all` inside `Response`, whose field is `headers`: 240), a parameter (`fd::`), a function (`assert::`) or a variable - every one then ignored by `stamp_module_scope` (`symbol_names_type` false) and answered by the module lane, but `record_resolution` had already sent the LSP's go-to-definition to the field; 98 annotation heads (`node::…` under a parameter `node`) the site likewise ignored; **11 identifiers in CALLEE position naming a CLASS** (`Node(1)`, `Parser(…)`), stamped `Def` today and answered by `resolve_direct_call` through the type stamp (`spelling_type`) - the value namespace refuses a `Type` symbol, so under `resolve_path` these are E0202 |
| `DIFF` | 32 | the annotation's generic-parameter probe: an enum VARIANT declared bare in the module scope (`JsonValue::String`, `::Array`) shadows the IMPORT of the same leaf; the site asked only "is it a generic parameter" and both say no, and the leaf lane then resolved the import from the module scope |
| `FIL-ONLY` | **0** | the filter never bound past a refused nearer rib to a different declaration |

So the namespace filter changes no stamp on the corpus except the 11
constructor calls, and those are a language-model question, not a
resolver's: Rust binds a tuple struct's constructor in the VALUE namespace
beside the type - two bindings, one declaration - and this symbol table
binds one `Type` symbol and cannot tell a class from a struct.  **§9 Q13.**

#### What is there now

* `resolve_type_qualified_name_bare_from` is deleted.  Its two callers ask
  `leaf_in_module_scope(module_scope, name)` on the `NameResolver`, which
  calls `resolve_path(&[name], Namespace::Type, ScopeID { id })` and stamps
  the `Def` it answers DIRECTLY - a walk from a module scope crosses no rib
  binding a generic parameter, so the answer is a definition or nothing,
  and nothing is `Pending` as before.  The string projection was one
  `DefId::of_definition(q.qualified_name())` round trip (`DEFID_UNWRAP` 32
  → 31, `DEFID_MINT` 23 → 21).  A pure refactor by construction: the
  function answered a string exactly when `resolve_path` answered `Def`.
* The other seven `lookup` sites and `bare_name_res` are NOT converted.
  The shape that makes `resolve_path` the one door is recorded here and
  not built: (1) `resolve_path` records the span's binding for the LSP
  (`record_resolution`), since seven of the nine sites exist to feed the
  resolution map and a `Res` carries no `SymbolID`; (2) `res_for_head`
  absorbs `bare_name_res`'s classification - `Local` for a parameter and
  a function-local variable, nothing for a member kind (a method, field
  or variant symbol is named through its owner, and `module::leaf` is a
  name nothing is registered under); (3) Q13's ruling for the constructor
  call; (4) the annotation lane's two scopes - the rib chain for a generic
  parameter, the writer's MODULE scope for the leaf, because annotations
  are re-resolved under other modules' cursors - become one explicit scope
  when the site passes the annotation's own rib.  Each is measurable with
  this entry's instrument; none is a unit on its own.

### 8.240 A placed specialization has ONE registrar: the monomorphizer registers the type, its bare-name mapping, the methods it carries and its impl blocks' at the seam, and the pass registers nothing for a named specialization - its four `register_methods` calls found every method already registered (190,183 of 218,521 over six halves) or skipped by the same guard at both writers (28,338: self-returning defaults, and `Result<T, E>::as_ref` whose return is unresolved at either moment) - 2026-09-17

#### What was there

§8.238 moved the specialized TYPE's registration to the monomorphizer's
seam and left the methods where they were: `SpecInjector::register`'s
struct / union / class arms registering the clone's inline methods,
`register_spec`'s loop registering each cloned impl block's, and the
bare-name mapping (`register_name_mapping(spec_name, arena_qname)`), all
in the pass that walks the entries after the module's monomorphization.
Two writers for one placed entry - and since §8.238 the pass's write of
every generic-method spec materialized at the walk was a second
registration of an entry already stamped.

Audit 11's "dead index API" was checked on the way here and is not dead:
`global_slot` is the private funnel of six live accessors
(`is_global_thread_local`, `global_extern_symbol`, `find_global_in_
namespace`, `find_global_by_qualified`, `record_global_extern_symbol`,
`mark_global_thread_local` - 2/2/2/1/2/1 external readers); `resolved_or`
and `lookup_qualified_alternatives` are the LSP's `bare_alts` lane, LIVE by
the ruling on §0's two `bare_alts` rows and pinned there.  The stale
`module_types` comment went in §8.236.  Nothing to delete; the audit's
§7 item is retired by this paragraph.

#### Measured

The seam registering everything the entry carries, the pass's
registrations kept, and a print at each of the pass's four
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.240/shadow.patch` over `5a464de4`, `corpus2.sh
w2`, `.objcmp/w2-lines.txt`, **218,521** `PM` lines, `failing halves: 0`,
`OVERALL PASS … projects: 64 passed`; `awk -F'\t' '$3=="PM"' | cut -f4,5,7
| sort | uniq -c`):

| at the pass | rows | |
|---|---:|---|
| `ALREADY` - the method carries the entry registration stamps | **190,183** | 156,875 impl-block methods, 32,761 struct inline, 2 union inline (registered at the seam); 545 generic-method specs (registered at the walk, §8.238) |
| `NEW`, self-returning default | 19,980 | `register_methods_by_key` skips `is_self_returning_default` at EVERY writer - a deferred template instantiated per call site - so neither the seam nor the pass registers one |
| `NEW`, return type unresolved | 8,358 | every one `Result<T, E>::as_ref(&this) -> Result<T*, E*>` (`SEAM` rows: 8,358, all `as_ref`, trait empty): the clone's return annotation names its own template over pointer arguments and is unresolved both at the seam and when the pass walks the entry; the guard (`!resolved_return_type.is_valid()` → `continue`) skips it at both, so the pass registered nothing here either.  `Option<T>::as_ref -> Option<T*>` does not appear: the one-parameter self-instantiation resolves.  Pre-existing and outside this entry: no `Result::as_ref` call exists in the corpus, and a control that makes one (`.objcmp/asref-ctl`, `Result<i32, i32>::as_ref` then `*v + 1`) builds and exits 42 under this tree, the previous half and the pin, so the method binds by a route this entry did not measure |
| `NEW`, anything else | **0** | |

So the pass's four registrations wrote nothing the seam had not.

#### What is there now

* The seam (`Monomorphizer::specialize_request`, after `resolve_specialized_ast`,
  before the entry is pushed) registers the type (§8.238), the bare-name
  mapping, the clone's inline methods (`register_carried_methods`) and
  each kept impl block's methods, all under the type.
* `SpecInjector::register(node, spec_type, ctx)` registers a placed
  specialization with NO named type - a function template's clone - as an
  injected declaration, and nothing for a named one; the `spec_name`
  parameter is gone with the mapping.  `register_spec` still rewrites each
  clone's impl head to the qualified spec name, records `spec_owner`, and

  generic registry - a registry write, not an index one, and one whose
  timing the selector reads (a placed clone applies outright), so it is
  deliberately NOT moved with the index writes.
* The lane gate's `REGISTER` total is unmoved at 66: the mapping's
  name-keyed write moved file (`specialization` 2 → 1, `monomorphizer`
  1 → 2), re-pinned.

### 8.241 Every declaration-holding store is under the lane gate's rule: a store is what the context carries, a name-keyed method is any a store declares in any file with `SymbolStr` or `string` in its signature, and a call is placed by its receiver's declared type - eight per-store rows, three audit mutations the old gate accepted and the new one refuses, a committed self-test of seventeen - 2026-09-17

> **Status:** LANDED.  `scripts/lane-gate.py` rewritten under three
> definition-derived rules; `tests/lane-baseline.txt` re-pinned at 18
> buckets; `scripts/lane-gate-selftest.py` in `check-fast`; §0.2 gains a row
> per store and one for the context's members that are not stores; §0.3's
> `lane-check` row rewritten and `lane-selftest` added; §5.2's and §7's
> status blocks say eighteen; §0's two corrupted cells (D5, the trait-registry
> row) restored.  No compiler source changed.

#### Why

Audit round 12 measured the old model 93% gutted and the new 78% complete,
and judged that eleven rounds had each found new surface for one reason:
every gate, row and shadow watched ONE store, `DeclarationIndex` (with
`TypeUtils` in front of it).  It proved three holes in `lane-gate`'s rule by
building the mutation each time:

1. **A cross-file `implement struct` block is invisible.**  The parser read
   the `type struct` block's inline methods only.  Cryo lets a method be
   added to a type from another file (`implement struct Point { ... }` in
   `docs/cryo.md`; three `implement struct` blocks in the stdlib), so a
   reader declared that way is outside the set.  0 such blocks in
   `compiler/src` - a control, not a guarantee.
2. **The key type is a token match.**  `NAME_TYPE = "SymbolStr"`, so a
   reader keyed by `string` is outside the set, and the index already took
   `string` parameters (`impl_owner(node, site: string)`).
3. **Every other store is invisible by construction.**  `GenericRegistry`
   held 22 name-keyed methods and 87 external sites under the gate's own
   rule, and §8.233 moved trait-impl selection into it; nothing enumerated
   it.

#### The three rules

The old gate had one definition-derived rule (which methods, §8.230) and two
lists: the store (one, by name) and the receiver spellings (`di`,
`*.decl_index`, `types`, `*.types`, `this`, `arena`, `*.arena`, `*_arena`).
Every list is the same hole as the `lookup_*` name pattern §8.230 removed.
Now:

* **A store is a declaration-holding type the `CompilationContext` carries
  by pointer**, plus `TypeUtils`.  The context's members were measured under
  the method rule one by one (`.objcmp/`-free; the inventory script is
  reproduced by `lane-gate.py --names` for the stores and was run over the
  rest by hand):

  | type | methods under the rule | external sites | store? |
  |---|---|---|---|
  | `DeclarationIndex` | 55 (52 `SymbolStr` + `impl_owner`, `type_of_decl`, `register_methods` by `string`) | 224 | yes (LOOKUP / LOOKUP_OTHER / REGISTER) |
  | `TypeUtils` | 11 (9 + `def_type`, `type_display_name`) | 61 | yes, the funnel (LOOKUP_ROUTED) |
  | `TypeArena` | 29 (21 `SymbolStr` + 8 display formatters returning `string`) | 125 | yes (LOOKUP_ARENA / ARENA_READ / ARENA_WRITE) |
  | `GenericRegistry` | 23 (22 + `is_wellknown_trait_path(s: string)`) | 92 | yes (REGISTRY_READ / REGISTRY_WRITE) |
  | `ModuleGraph` | 6 (4 + `find_module_by_path`, `paths_equal_ignore_case`) | 32 | yes (GRAPH_READ / GRAPH_WRITE) |
  | `ConstantTable` | 4 (`register`, `register_enum`, two static key helpers) | 5 | yes (CONST_READ / CONST_WRITE).  **Audit 12 wrote `ConstTable 0`: the type is `ConstantTable`, so its zero was over the wrong population** |
  | `Resolver` | 33 | 11 on a `Resolver` receiver outside `compiler/resolver/`, `instance.cryo`, `compilation_context.cryo` | yes, as REENTRY: an ask from outside the pass is the re-entry §7.2 names |
  | `InternTable` | 4 (every one, by construction) | 1,622 by name | **no** - it holds strings, not declarations; it IS the boundary |
  | `TypeResolver` | 11 | 18 | **no** - pointers to the stores above and no table; a name it answers it answers by asking one of them |
  | `Monomorphizer` / `MonoState` | 7 / 5 | 10 / 10 (all `this.state`) | **no** - spec bookkeeping keyed by mangled symbol, a stamp derivation |
  | `TypeChecker` | 3 (`check_binary_op(op: string)`) | 5 | **no** - an operator spelling, no table |
  | `ModuleLoader` / `PhaseArtifacts` | 24 / 1 | 9 / 3 | **no** - keyed by filesystem path |
  | `DirectiveRegistry` | 3 (`has(kind: string)`) | - | **no** - keyed by directive kind |

  Each exclusion is stated in the script beside `STORES`.  [The sentence
  that stood here - "so the next type added to the context is a question the
  script asks rather than one an audit finds" - was FALSE of the script:
  `STORES` was a hand-written dict of seven that the script never checked
  against the tree, so a new store was exactly what an audit finds, and
  audit 13 found one (`DefaultRegistry`) by adding a map-keyed member to the
  context and reading OK.  §8.253 derives the store list from the tree.]

* **A name-keyed method is any a store declares - in its `type struct`
  block or in an inherent `implement [<G>] [struct] Store {` block in ANY
  file - whose signature mentions `SymbolStr` or `string` as a whole
  token.**  The widening sweeps in `string` parameters that are labels
  rather than keys (`impl_owner(node, site: string)`,
  `type_of_decl(d: DefId, site: string)`) and `string` returns that are
  display text (`format_display`, `resolve_display_name`).  They are pinned
  like keys: the rule cannot tell a label from a key and does not try, and
  a row that moves for one of them is explained at the re-pin like any
  other.  The alternative - a list of parameter names to ignore - is the
  hole again.

* **A call is placed by its receiver's DECLARED TYPE.**  `this` is the
  enclosing `type`/`implement` block's type; a bare identifier is what its
  nearest preceding annotation says (a parameter, a `const`/`mut` binding,
  a field - a struct-literal initializer's lowercase token is skipped);
  each `.field` is the field's declaration; `x()` is the method's declared
  return type; `x[...]` is the element type.  All read from the tree.  A
  receiver any hop of which cannot be read is a hard failure, as before.
  Over the real tree the placer refused three receivers on its first run -
  `this.get_arena().resolve_display_name(…)`, `this.scopes[i].is_ambiguous(…)`,
  `pm_prior: build_manifest::ModuleKeyTable` - each a grammar it did not yet
  read, none a store under a new alias; the accessor, index and qualified
  forms were added and it places every call in the tree.  A set name on a
  receiver whose type is NOT a store lands in `LOOKUP_LOCAL`, which is now
  the control on placement: all 59 were read by eye
  (`FunctionRegistry.register` 9, `ScopeManager.restore_scope` 7 /
  `lookup_local` 5, `DropInserter.lookup_type` 5, `MoveChecker.lookup_type`
  4, `OwnershipQuery::qualified_name_of` 4, `GlobalRegistry.register` 4,
  `DeclarationEmitter.declare_method` 4 / `declare_function` 1,
  `SpecializationPasses::register_inherent_owner` 3 / `register_impl_block`
  1, `DefaultRegistry.lookup` 2 / `register` 1, `TypeMapperCache.lookup`,
  `TraitChecker.template_key_of` 2, `MonoTraitSpecializer.template_key_of`,
  `Scope.is_ambiguous`, `Parser.enter_scope`, `ModuleKeyTable.lookup`,
  `SpecInjector::register`, `AsyncLower.declare_method`), every one a
  same-named method on a type that holds no declarations of the program.

`REENTRY`'s field-reached half was a three-name list (`set_module`,
`find_module_scope`, `restore_scope`, §8.189).  It is now the `Resolver`'s
whole set under the method rule, on a `Resolver`-typed receiver outside the
resolver's directory and the two driver files (`compilation_context.cryo`
joins `instance.cryo`: its `switch_to_module` moves the cursor for the
driver).  Predicted before the run: 6 → 12, mono 3 unmoved, sema 2 → 5
(three asks on the `get_resolver()` local), `dead_code` 1, `types/resolver.cryo`
+2, `passes/type_resolution.cryo` +1.  Measured: exactly that.  The two in
`types/resolver.cryo` are a finding: `resolve_named` asks
`this.name_resolver.is_ambiguous(name)` and `get_ambiguous_modules(name)` by
SPELLING - type resolution reading the name resolver's ambiguity table under
a bare leaf to render E0155's "imported from two modules" - a spelling ask
no list named and no row counted.  Recorded, not moved; it is diagnostic
text, and the entry that converts it should say what stamp the annotation
carries at that point.  The one in `type_resolution.cryo` is
`Resolver::ns_written_as(mod_str, written)`, a static string comparison
asking whether a module's canonical name was written as a given spelling.

#### What this gate still cannot see

* A receiver placed by the NEAREST PRECEDING annotation of its name: a
  local re-declared under the same name with a different type in an earlier
  function of the same file would be placed by the nearer, wrong one.  The
  placement control (`LOOKUP_LOCAL` read by eye) is what catches a store

  fails.
* A store reached through a call with arguments (`ctx.registry_for(m).get_template(…)`)
  is refused, not placed; the tree holds none.
* A `string` that is a label.  Pinned as a key, said above.
* What it always could not: a lane that ANSWERS.  Source text only.

### 8.242 The async receiver-refresh decision reads the trait off the projection's owning trait, not off a first-match scan by the method's leaf: `desugar_async_trait_methods` stamps the trait on `This::<Method>Fut` at birth, `GenericRegistry::trait_decl_of(TypeRef)` answers the declaration by identity, `TypeArena::get_qualified_name` gains the `Trait` arm it lacked; the scan disagreed at 4 of 11 unit-suite sites (`Read` for `AtmRead::read`, `GfTick` for `GenTick::tick`) and 0 of 28 example sites, and the consequence - a dropped refresh - is unobservable: every generic-receiver refresh dropped leaves 142 + 17 + 3 async tests green, because a carried receiver's storage does not move between polls - 2026-09-17

> **Status:** LANDED.  Compiler: `passes/type_resolution.cryo`,
> `sema/async_lower.cryo`, `types/generic_registry.cryo`, `types/arena.cryo`.
> `find_trait_defining_method` keeps ONE reader, sema's "defined on trait Y"
> hint.  `lane-check` `REGISTRY_READ` 69 → 67, `ARENA_READ` 75 → 76,
> re-pinned.  §0.2's registry and arena rows updated.

#### The shape

```cryo
type trait Write      { flush(mut &this); }            // registered first
type trait AsyncWrite { async flush(mut &this); }      // registered later

type struct BufStream<S> {
    inner: S;
    async flush_all(mut &this) -> void where S: AsyncWrite {
        await this.inner.flush();      // S::FlushFut - which trait?
    }
}
```

At `await this.inner.flush()` the receiver's type is the bare parameter
`S`, so the callee is unresolved (`resolved_method` needs a concrete owner)
and the awaited type is the projection `S::FlushFut` that
`desugar_async_trait_methods` minted for the trait method.  The lowering has
to decide whether the sub-future stores a receiver pointer to re-address
before each poll (`awaited_keeps_recv_ptr`), and answered it by
`find_trait_defining_method(mname)`: the FIRST registered trait declaring
any method of that leaf, then a loop over that trait's `is_async` methods.
`Write` registers before `AsyncWrite` in `stdlib/io/traits.cryo`, so the
loop found nothing and the refresh was dropped.  Audit 12's item 2.

#### The root

The projection carried no identity: `create_assoc_projection(this_ty,
assoc, TypeRef::invalid())` - "invalid = infer" - although the desugar held
the `TraitDeclNode` and the trait's type (`type_of_decl(node.def)`) was
computed four lines later.  Now `desugar_async_trait_methods(node, ctx,
arena, trait_ref)` mints the projection with `owning_trait = trait_ref`;
`method_binding.cryo:549` and `substitution.cryo:262` already carry
`owning_trait` through the `This → S` substitution, so it reaches the await
site (shadow: `ot_valid=1` at all 39 sites).  The reader asks
`GenericRegistry::trait_decl_of(ap.owning_trait)` - the registry holds trait
declarations under the same identity the arena holds the trait's type
(`decl_type_key(node.name, "", file)` at both `pass_registry.cryo:940` and
`type_resolution.cryo:2832`), so the type answers the declaration through
the reverse map.  No reader of `AssocProjectionType.owning_trait` exists in
resolution or mono (`grep -rn 'owning_trait' compiler/src`: the arena's dedup
key, two carry-throughs, and the AST's separate `SymbolStr` field), so a
valid trait changes no resolution.

**The reverse map could not name a trait.**  The first shadow answered
`NEWNULL` at all 78 lines: `get_qualified_name` had arms for struct, class,
enum, instantiation and alias, and `_ => {}` for a `TraitType` that carries
`qualified_name`.  Added.  A count at the new arm over examples + the unit
suite: 39 asks, exactly the reader's 39 - no caller had ever asked the
arena to name a trait, so nothing that took the empty answer changes.

#### The shadow (`.objcmp/s1-lines.txt`, `scripts/ns-migration/8.242/`)

One line per reader call, the scan beside the identity, over the 14
examples (built by hand; `make examples` builds nothing on this host) and
the unit suite (`cryo test async`, which compiles the whole suite):

| corpus | sites | SAME | DIFF |
|---|---|---|---|
| examples | 28 | 28 | 0 |
| unit suite | 11 | 7 | 4 |

The four: `async_receiver_refresh.cryo:171 tick` (scan `GfTick`, a sync
`tick(mut &this)` in `async_generic_function.cryo`, registered first by file
order; identity `GenTick`), `async_trait_method.cryo:94` and `:191 read`
(scan `std::io::traits::Read`; identity `AtmRead`), `io_async_traits.cryo:173
read_exact` (scan `Read`; identity `AsyncRead`).  Audit 12 reported 15
entries / 8 disagreeing over the same suite: a wrong answer makes
`emit_recv_refresh` ask a second time through `expr_has_recv_call`, so each
DIFF printed twice - 7 + 2×4 = 15, 2×4 = 8.  Reconciled.

#### The consequence, measured: unreachable

The brief asked for a repro where the frame moves and something reads
through the stale pointer.  Built (`.objcmp/tick-ctl/`, the shape above
with `GenTick::tick(mut &this)` writing `this.hits` after a suspend and a
sync `SyncTick` declared first):

* a driver polling from a DIFFERENT stack depth on every poll: **33**, the
  write lands.  The IR says why: the receiver `c` is not a block-local but
  the frame's own field, reached by `unwrap_ptr` (§8's in-place carrier),
  so `&frame.c.inner` is the same address on every poll.
* a driver MOVING the future after every `Pending`: refused, **E0459**
  "future 'g' is moved after it has been polled … polled here, fixing its
  address".  The frame cannot move between polls.

So the two ways a receiver's storage could move are closed by construction:
an aggregate local is built in its carrier field and never leaves it
(`promote_cross_state`: "the value never left"), a `mut` scalar is
rewritten to its field in place, a parameter is carried the same way, and
the frame itself is address-fixed once polled.  The refresh's own comment
("an owning receiver promoted across states still lives in a fresh
block-local on every poll") described the mechanism the in-place carrier
replaced; corrected to the invariant.

The instrument: `awaited_keeps_recv_ptr` answering `false` on the
projection path always - every generic-receiver refresh dropped, the scan's
worst case at every site - built and run over the async suite
(`.objcmp/m2-test.log`): `OVERALL PASS (unit: ok; compile-fail: 17
passed; projects: 3 passed)`, 142 unit tests passed, 0 failed.  The
receiver-refresh test file's own generic-owner tests, whose comments say
the write "is simply never seen again" without the refresh, pass without
it.  A first, broader mutation (answering `false` on the concrete path too)
failed the suite's BUILD with an E0455 at `async_pointer_across_await.cryo:
145` - a true answer there feeds a carry decision, not only the store - so
the concrete path is not redundant and was not the question.

**What the wrong answer did change**, silently: the store itself (the
tick-ctl IR under `1f852403`'s compiler has no `store … this$recv` before
the resumed poll of the inner future; this tree's has one), and the two
E0455 refusals a true answer gates (a receiver naming no storage; a stored
method future awaited later), which no negative test exercises on a
generic receiver.  Both now answer by identity.

#### Objects and gates

`make lsp-check`: `OK -- compiled 264 module(s) … 0 errors, 490
warning(s)` (`.objcmp/u2-lsp.log`).  `make cross-check`: `OK --
x86_64-pc-linux-gnu … 0 errors` (`.objcmp/u2-cross.log`).  `make

### 8.243 `ns-status-check` refuses a §0 whose text has lost the shape a check is read by - a table row with more cells than its header, a check cell whose backticks do not pair once its checks are removed, a backticked command with no `→ **N**` - because the extractor matched `` `cmd` → **N** `` wherever it stood and skipped a damaged span for the next well-formed one: the two spliced cells audit 12 named passed it, and so did three checks that had NEVER run - their answer written `` `0` `` rather than `**0**` - which the rules found beyond the audit's two; all seven repaired, five self-test cases, and one migration script gains `--check` so a §0 row stops editing the tree - 2026-09-18

> **Status:** LANDED.  `scripts/ns_ledger.py` (`structural_problems`),
> `scripts/ns-status-check.py`, `scripts/ns-guard-selftest.py` (19 cases),
> `scripts/qualify-intrinsic-calls.py` (`--check`).  §0: seven cells
> repaired; `ns-status-check` reads **278** rows where it read 274 before
> the two cells the audit named were restored (§8.241) and 276 after -
> the four rows that had never run, run.

#### The hole

`ROW_RE` is `` `([^`]+)`\s*→\s*\*\*([^*]+)\*\*``, applied to §0's text with
`findall`.  It matches the shape wherever it stands.  So a cell in which the
FIRST span was damaged - D5's, spliced at `fd3756af` by a sed pattern whose
`\|` was alternation (§8.234's handoff): `` `grep -rho 'x' compiler/src
\|`grep -rho -e … | wc -l` → **0** `` - is read as ONE valid check: the
damaged span is skipped and the next backticked span with an arrow is taken.
D5's check stopped running, the trait-registry row's check ran twice, and
the gate said `OK -- 274 row(s)`.  A gate that cannot see its own corruption
is the shape this suite paid for before (`resolve_counter`'s zero, the
inert commit hook): it looks installed.

#### The rules (`ns_ledger.structural_problems`)

Run before any row, over §0's text line by line:

1. **Cell count.**  A table row must have as many cells as its table's
   header row (cells split on an UNESCAPED pipe).  The splice above brought
   an unescaped `| wc -l` with it - an extra column - and a pattern fragment
   pasted into the trait-registry row (`**5**|heads_for(&this\|trait_…`) did
   the same.  A row that fails this is reported once and not read further:
   its cells cannot be told apart.
2. **Pairing.**  In any cell or bullet line holding an arrow, remove every
   well-formed `` `cmd` → **N** ``; the backticks left must pair.  An
   unpaired one is a span that lost its end - D5's `` `grep … \| ``.
3. **A command with no answer.**  Any span still paired that begins with a
   command word (`grep`, `git`, `python3`, `awk`, `sed`, `wc`, … - the
   grammar §0's checks are written in, POSIX one-liners, not a list a
   reader depends on) is a check that lost its `→ **N**`.  A note's
   backticked NAMES after a value (`(8 when this was written; `HOME_WRITE`
   since §8.204)`) pair and are not commands: allowed, and a self-test case
   says so.

Rule 2 and 3 look at any piece with an ARROW, not `→ **`: a first cut looked
for `→ **` and read OK over a cell whose ONLY check had its answer in
backticks - the cell that has never run is exactly the one with no `→ **`
in it.  Caught by the self-test's own case before it landed.

#### What the rules found: seven, not two

Over `1f852403`'s §0 (`.objcmp/`-free: `scripts/ns-migration/8.243/corrupt.py`
regenerates each shape from the current ledger) and over HEAD's after
§8.241's two restorations:

| §0 line | row | shape | ran before? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 50 | D5 | spliced cell, extra column (audit 12) | the registry's check ran twice; D5's not at all |
| 109 | trait-impl registry | pasted fragment, two extra columns (audit 12) | the `select_impl` check ran twice |
| 51 | D6 | `` → `0 rewritten` `` - the answer in backticks | **never** |
| 119 | `HOME_WRITE` row | `` → `TOTAL 0` `` | **never** |
| 134 | `is_alias_keyword` row | unescaped `\| wc -l`, an extra column | yes (the span still paired) |
| 141 | `qualified_target_name` row | two unescaped pipes, two extra columns | yes |
| 240 | §0.3's CI bullet | `` → `main` only, both hooks `` | **never** |

The three that never ran are the finding beyond the audit: `ns-status-check`
counted them as prose.  D6's is also a check with a SIDE EFFECT - it ran a
migration script (`qualify-intrinsic-calls.py`) that rewrites the file it
scans when it finds anything; `--check` counts and writes nothing, and the
row reads `→ **0**` off its last token.  The `HOME_WRITE` row now reads its
golden total the way §8.241's rows do (`grep -A1 … \| grep -o '[0-9]*$'`);
the CI bullet counts `branches: [main]` (2, both hooks) and `branches:` (2,
no others).  The two unescaped pipes are escaped.

#### The pairs (`scripts/ns-migration/8.243/ns-pair.sh`, log `.objcmp/ns-pair.log`)

`9e7b778b`'s gate beside this one, over a copy of the current ledger with
one corruption re-applied at a time, the row commands running against the
same tree under both:

| ledger | old gate | new gate |
|---|---|---|
| the current one (control) | `OK -- 276 row(s)` | `OK -- 276 row(s)` |
| D5's cell as spliced | **`OK -- 276 row(s)`** | `MALFORMED CHECK … table row has 6 cell(s), its header has 5` |
| the trait-registry fragment | **`OK -- 277 row(s)`** | `MALFORMED … 7 cell(s), its header has 5` |
| D6's answer in backticks | **`OK -- 275 row(s)`** | `MALFORMED … a command with no `→ **expected**`` |
| the unescaped pipe | **`OK -- 276 row(s)`** | `MALFORMED … 6 cell(s), its header has 5` |

(The control reads 276 because the pair ran before the CI bullet was
repaired; 278 after.)  The old gate's row COUNT moves with each corruption -
276, 277, 275 - and it reports OK at every one of them: the count was the
only trace, and nothing read it.

`ns-guard-selftest.py` gains five cases driven through the guard on a real
commit: the splice, the backticked answer, the unescaped pipe, a second
command in a note with no answer (refused), and a note whose backticked
spans are names (allowed).  Each refusal is pinned to its reason by
`saying`, because the row-count floor refuses a damaged fixture too, for
the wrong reason - which is what the first run of the backticked-answer
case did, and what led to the `→` widening above.  The self-test now
decodes the guard's output as UTF-8 (it read the arrow as cp1252 and no
`saying` with an arrow could match).

#### Gates

`make ns-status-check`: `OK -- 278 §0 row(s)`; `make guard-selftest`: `OK
-- 19 case(s)`; `make check-fast` OK.  No compiler source changed.

Twice this unit a background job's log was read STALE: the poll loop's

### 8.244 A bare type name two imports tie for names neither, on the annotation lane as on the identifier lane: `resolve_path` answers `Err` for a head an ambiguous import binds (the rib bound it, to nothing, and the walk stops there), the name layer refuses it where it was written (E0154, stamped `Err`), and the type resolver's arm that asked the resolver's CURSOR scope `is_ambiguous(name)` by spelling - the two `REENTRY` sites §8.241's rule surfaced - is deleted; the annotation lane bound such a name silently to whichever import came first (a control: bare `Cursor` from `std::io::cursor` and `std::net::http2::hpack` compiled and read `io::Cursor`'s fields), and 0 such binds exist in six halves - 2026-09-18

> **Status:** LANDED.  `resolver/resolver.cryo` (`resolve_path`,
> `ambiguous_modules_from`), `resolver/name_resolution.cryo`
> (`leaf_in_module_scope`), `types/resolver.cryo` (the arm deleted), a
> negative test.  `lane-check` `REENTRY` 12 → 10, `LOOKUP_LOCAL` 59 → 60
> (`sc.is_ambiguous` on a `Scope`, the rib's own record), re-pinned.

#### The shape

```cryo
import std::io::cursor::{ Cursor };
import std::net::http2::hpack::{ Cursor };   // a second Cursor, different module

function takes(c: Cursor) -> i32 {           // which one?
    return c.pos as i32;
}
```

Under `9e7b778b` this compiled, exit 0, and `c` was `std::io::cursor::Cursor`
(`c.buffer.length` compiled too; `c.nonexistent_field` was refused naming
that type).  The scope keeps the FIRST import of a tied leaf "so lookups
still find SOMETHING" and records the tie (`Scope::insert_import`); the
identifier lane reads the record (`visit(IdentifierNode*)`, E0154 "`alloc`
is ambiguous", `tests/negative/E0154_ambiguous_bare_call.cryo`) and the
annotation lane never did: `leaf_in_module_scope` asks `resolve_path`, the
rib walk finds the first import and `res_for_head` stamps it.  §4 rule 2 -
"two imported modules both exporting `Foo` is ambiguous" - held for a value
and not for a type.

#### The root, and the arm it retires

`Resolver::resolve_path`'s rib walk: a head bound by an `Import` symbol in a
rib whose record ties it (`sc.is_ambiguous(head)`, the RIB's record, not the
cursor's chain) answers `Res::Err`, and the walk stops - the rib did bind
the head, to nothing, and rule 1 says an inner tier's binding shadows the
outer one.  `leaf_in_module_scope(module_scope, name, span)` then asks the
written scope's chain for the tie (`Resolver::ambiguous_modules_from(scope,
name)`, the explicit-scope form `get_ambiguous_modules` now delegates to)
and refuses with E0154 in the identifier lane's words, labelled "ambiguous
type name", stamping `Res::Err`; the type layer reports nothing for an
`Err`-stamped leaf ("reported once whichever pass asks",
`extract_unresolved_named`).

`TypeResolver::resolve_named`'s "2b. Ambiguity check" asked
`this.name_resolver.is_ambiguous(name)` and `get_ambiguous_modules(name)` -
the CURSOR's scope chain, by the leaf's spelling, after the stamp path had
missed - and emitted E0203 "ambiguous type" from it.  For a stamped
annotation it could never fire (the stamp hits first); for an unstamped
one it answered from wherever the cursor stood, which is B1's shape.  The
first cut of this fix showed it live: with `resolve_path` answering `Err`
and the leaf left `Pending`, the control produced THREE reports - the
arm's E0203, `type_resolution.cryo:670`'s E0155 "declared in more than one
module", and nothing under E0154.  Deleted; the two `REENTRY` sites go with
it.

#### Measured

The shadow (`scripts/ns-migration/8.244/shadow.patch`, a print at the new
`Err` arm) over six halves - the 14 examples, the unit suite (`cryo test
async`, whole-suite compile), `make lsp-check` (stdlib + compiler + LSP
under the stage-2 compiler), `make cross-check` (the other OS's gated
half): **0 lines**.  The control (`.objcmp/amb-ctl`, the shape above)
prints one: `AMBPATH Cursor AmbCtl std::io::cursor std::net::http2::hpack`.
No annotation in the tree binds through a tied import; the blast radius of
refusing it is the control alone.  (`cryo test --list` was tried first and
prints nothing because it parses without resolving - the count was taken

(194 negatives).

#### The shape

Bucket A of audit 12's id-move is a reader that already holds the name
layer's answer and turns it back into a string to ask a store:

```cryo
// before: the id unwrapped at the reader, the store asked by the name
Res::Def(q) => { stamp_key = q.qualified_name(); }
stamp_hit = this.decl_index.lookup_type(stamp_key);
if (!stamp_hit.is_valid()) { stamp_hit = this.arena.lookup_by_name(stamp_key); }

// after: the id handed over; the unwrap lives in the store's door
Res::Def(q) => { stamp = q; }
stamp_hit = this.decl_index.type_of_def(stamp);
```

The doors already existed for a type and a function (`type_of_def`,
`func_type_of_def`, the `_of_res` pair, §8.219); a global gets its sibling
here, `global_of_def(d, intern)`, which is `find_global_by_qualified` with
the split of the canonical name into the slot's `(leaf, namespace)` moved
inside the index beside `split_global_key` - the one caller unwrapped an id
to feed it and dropped the module it handed back.

The seven sites, each with what it asked before:

| site | asked before | asks now |
|---|---|---|
| `TypeUtils::def_global` | `find_global_by_qualified(q.qualified_name(), …)` | `global_of_def(q, …)` |
| `TypeUtils::scope_qualifier_type`, the `Def` arm | `q = d.qualified_name()` … `lookup_type_exact(q)` | `type_of_def(d)` |
| `TypeResolver::resolve_named` 2c, the stamp | `lookup_type(q.qualified_name())`, then the arena by the same name | `type_of_def(q)`; no arena |
| `CallResolver::resolve_direct_call` | `types.lookup_func_return(r.def_id().qualified_name())` | `overload_return_type(func_type_of_res(r))` |
| `Sema` function-as-value | `generic_registry.get_template(def_q)` | `template_of(r.def_id())` |
| `type_name_key` / `ann_canon_key` (the coherence key) | `lookup_type(stamped ?: name)` - the stamp's name, else the SPELLING | `type_of_def(q)` for a `Def`, `lookup_type(n)` for a `PrimTy`, nothing else |
| `PatternEmitter`, a constant pattern | `parent_of(q)` split by hand, `resolve_global_in_namespace(pat.value, ns)` | `resolve_global_by_qualified(d.qualified_name())` |

The last is codegen's own splitter beside the index's: `split_global_key`'s
comment said it was "the one place a canonical name is split back into the
slot's key, so sema and codegen cannot split it differently", and it was
not - the pattern emitter split with `QualifiedName::parent_of` and used
the WRITTEN leaf (`pat.value`) as the slot's leaf.  It is one place now.
`resolve_direct_call` read `func_returns`, a second map written in lockstep
with `func_type_refs` at all three writers (`decl_index.cryo:846/883`,
`:1064/1067`, `type_resolution.cryo:1514/1515`); the return type off the
stamped signature is the same answer from the one map.

> `register_function` deleted), `sema/type_utils.cryo` (the delegate
> deleted), `sema/call_resolver.cryo` (`family_return_type`, six callers;
> the rescue arm deleted), `scripts/lane-gate.py` and its self-test (four
> `LOOKUP` names), §7.2 mechanism 5.  `lane-check` `LOOKUP` 11 → 10,
> `REGISTER` 79 → 78, `LOOKUP_ROUTED` 59 → 54, re-pinned.

#### Why this and not more of bucket B

§8.245's shadow put the direct call's return on the stamped signature and
found `func_returns` answering nothing the signature did not.  Bucket B's
reader side is otherwise the `GenericRegistry` (§8.241: keys are canonical
strings off stamps), whose re-keying by identity is Jake's (§0's
trait-registry row), and its writer side is registration
(`decl_type_key` at the registrars, the `REGISTER` row), which the readers
precede.  A whole per-kind lookup name is the larger move on the reader
side, and it was measured already.

#### The shape

```cryo
// before: two maps, one key, written together everywhere
this.func_returns.insert(name.id, return_type);          // register_function
this.func_type_refs.insert(name.id, func_type_ref);      // register_signature
// ... and read as if they could differ
pinned_ft = di.lookup_func_type(fam);
if (!pinned_ft.is_valid()) {                             // "a family registered
    const spec_ret = types.lookup_func_return(fam);      //  with a return alone"
    if (spec_ret.is_valid()) { return spec_ret; }
}

// after: one map; the return is the signature's
family_return_type(&this, family: SymbolStr) -> TypeRef {
    return this.overload_return_type(this.types.lookup_func_type_exact(family));
}
```

The writers, each pair adjacent: `decl_index.cryo` `register_methods`
(`register_function(combined_sym, ret)` then `register_signature(
combined_sym, get_function(ret, …))`), `register_function_signature`
(both under `name`), `type_resolution.cryo`'s clone arm (both under
`func.name`).  No writer touched one map without the other, and no reset
touched either.  `register_function_signature` keeps its `return_type`
parameter for the mangling.

### 8.247 TemplateRegistration keys a type's template, its static-method templates and its inherent-owner entry by the declaration's stamp, and reads the base type from the index by that id: `register_generic_template` takes the `DefId` the type-declaration stage stamped, `register_static_method_templates` and `register_inherent_owner` take the owner's registered key, and the three `decl_type_key(name, <no namespace>, file)` re-derivations go - the last of which registered every C-imported type's inherent owner under a key the type is not registered by (`FfiCImport::CImportTest::Bits` for `cit::Bits`, 7 in the corpus) - and with the arena no longer asked a type by name anywhere in the compiler, `TypeArena::lookup_by_name` and the lane gate's `LOOKUP_ARENA` row are deleted - 2026-09-18

> **Status:** LANDED.  `passes/specialization.cryo` (the three registrars
> and their seven callers), `types/arena.cryo` (`lookup_by_name` deleted),
> `scripts/lane-gate.py` and its self-test (17 buckets; the arena's
> parser control is `store_methods`' own non-empty check, and a name lookup
> added to the arena under any spelling lands in `ARENA_READ`).
> `lane-check` `LOOKUP_ARENA` 1 → row deleted, `DEFID_UNWRAP` 27 → 31 (four
> registry keys read off a stamp in place of a re-derivation, as §8.228's
> three), re-pinned.

#### Why this

Bucket B's registration side: a key derived from a declaration in hand,
where the declaration already carries the id its registration returned
(§8.225: the six type-declaration nodes carry `def`).  TemplateRegistration
runs after the TypeDeclaration stage, so the stamp is there to read.

```cryo
// before: the key re-derived from the spelling and the file, the base
// type asked of the arena by that name
const qualified_sym = ctx.decl_type_key(name, SymbolStr::empty(), ast_node.span.file);
base_type = arena.lookup_by_name(qualified_sym);

// after: the stamp is the key and the index answers by it
const qualified_sym = def.qualified_name();
base_type = ctx.decl_index.type_of_def(def);
```

`register_static_method_templates(owner_key, methods, …)` and
`register_inherent_owner(owner_key, ast, registry)` take the owner's
registered key: a declaration's stamp from the three declaration arms, the
head's `target_key` from the impl-block arm (which had it in hand and
re-derived a second one from `node.target_type` and the impl's file).

### 8.248 D23's three refused-only arms are scoped: they are entered by exactly two shapes - a bare callee that binds to nothing (`resolve_direct_call`'s E0202, the allocator leaves included) and an undeclared name in an impl head's target argument (`Holder<S>`, type resolution's E0302) - so the arms cannot become doors until the name layer stamps `Err` on those two, which is the E0202 reporting move with its four context-dependent notes and the `FILE`/`LINE` magic names in front of it; measured, not built - 2026-09-18

> **Status:** MEASURED; nothing built.  The reporting move is a unit of its
> own and is left for the next worker with this scoping.

Probe (`scripts/ns-migration/8.247/d23_probe.py`, a print at each of the
three arms, every negative through `cryo check`; `.objcmp/w3-d23.txt`):
13 lines from 3 of 194 files.

| arm | entries | file | name |
|---|---|---|---|
| `find_fn_template_for_call` | 2 per callee | `E0202_undefined_function`, `E0202_bare_allocator_leaf` | `cf_does_not_exist`; `malloc`, `free`, `realloc` |
| `lookup_callee_function_type`'s hint | 1 per callee | the same two | the same four |
| `ann_canon_key`'s `Named` arm | 1 | `E0302_trait_head_undeclared_param` | `S` in `implement trait Tick for struct Holder<S>` |

Both call-resolver arms are one population: `visit(IdentifierNode*)`
leaves a bare name that binds to nothing `Pending` (`bare_name_res`
answers nothing and nothing is stamped), and sema reports it -
`resolve_direct_call`'s E0202 with three notes that need sema's context
(`generic_angle_guessed`, `collect_module_declarers_of_leaf`, the
did-you-mean over `collect_bare_callable_names`), or `Sema`'s E0201 for a
value with `collect_local_names`.  Before either, sema answers `FILE` and
`LINE` by their spelling (`sema.cryo`: `name_str.eq("FILE")`), so a name
layer that refused every unbound bare identifier would refuse those two
first.  The third arm is type resolution's: `S` is stamped by nothing and
E0302 is reported off the template's parameter count, which the name layer
does not have.

So the arms become doors only when: the name layer stamps `Res::Err` on an
unbound bare identifier and reports E0201/E0202 there (or leaves the
report to sema while stamping `Err`, which the `_ =>` arms then never see);
the magic names become declarations or a `Res` of their own; and an
undeclared head argument is stamped `Err` in the name layer with E0302's
report left where its count is.  That is the reporting move audit 11
called the largest diagnostic piece; the E0202 did-you-mean's empty
population is a separate, known gap and is not touched by it.

Outside the ledger: nothing (the probe is restored; its script rides in
`scripts/ns-migration/8.247/`).

### 8.249 The source-location pseudo-constants are the name layer's answer: a bare `FILE` or `LINE` that no scope binds is stamped `Res::SourceLoc(File | Line)` where it is written, as a primitive spelling is stamped `PrimTy` on the type lane, and the two consumers that recognised them by spelling - sema's identifier typing (`name_str.eq("FILE")`) and codegen's identifier emitter - read the kind off the stamp; 0 disagreements between spelling and stamp over the six halves, the control 1,374 and 1,112 on one example, 0 objects moved - 2026-09-18

> **Status:** LANDED.  `resolver/res.cryo` (`SourceLoc`, `Res::SourceLoc`),
> `resolver/name_resolution.cryo` (`visit(IdentifierNode*)`'s unbound
> arm), `sema/sema.cryo` (`resolve_identifier`), `codegen/visit/
> ir_generator.cryo` (`codegen_identifier`).  The first step of the
> E0201/E0202 reporting move §8.248 scoped: a name layer that refuses
> every unbound bare identifier must first answer the two that are
> unbound by design.

#### Why this

`FILE` and `LINE` are declared nowhere (`grep -rnE '(const|mut|function|
struct|enum|type|class)\s+(FILE|LINE)\b'` over `stdlib compiler/src tests
examples tools` → 0) and used 281 times, every one as `panic`'s or
`assert`'s `FILE, LINE` pair.  The name layer's lookup missed them and
left the slot `Pending` with a comment saying a later stage would answer;
sema and codegen each answered by comparing the spelling, after every
other lookup had failed - which is the shadowing order a binding of the
same name would have, written twice.

```cryo
// before: Pending from the name layer; sema and codegen each ask the spelling
if (name_str.eq("FILE")) { return this.arena.get_string(); }   // sema
if (name_str.eq("FILE")) { … build_global_string_ptr(node.span.file …) }  // codegen

// after: one answer, from the layer whose job is spellings, read by kind
match (SourceLoc::of_spelling(written)) {            // name layer, lookup missed
    Option::Some(k) => { node.set_res(Res::SourceLoc(k)); return; }
    …
}
Res::SourceLoc(SourceLoc::File) => { this.arena.get_string() }   // sema
ResSlot::Answered(Res::SourceLoc(k)) => { match (k) { … node.span … } }  // codegen
```

The variant is a value-lane `PrimTy`: an answer for a spelling that
names a builtin and so binds in no scope.  It is asked only after every
scope has declined, so a declaration of the same name shadows it, as an
inner rib shadows an outer one.  The spelling is compared in exactly one
place (`SourceLoc::of_spelling`); a consumer switches on the kind.

Not a declaration in the prelude: the value a reference expands to is the
REFERENCE's file and line, which no declaration carries, and Cryo has no
declaration form for a compiler-expanded constant.  Rust's `file!()` is a
builtin macro declared in `core`; Cryo has no macro namespace, and the
spec (`docs/cryo.md` §4) states them as pseudo-constants the compiler
expands, which this encodes.

#### Measured

code): sema's identifier resolver and codegen's identifier emitter each
compare the old spelling test with the stamp and print `SRCLOC-DIFF` when
the two disagree.  `scripts/objcmp/corpus2.sh X1s` over the six halves
(`.objcmp/x1s-corpus.out`): `lsp direct exit=0`, `make test exit=0`,

#### The move

```cryo
cf_does_not_exist(1);        // before: Pending from the name layer, E0202 from sema
                             // after:  E0202 from the name layer, stamped Err
return cf_missing;           // E0201 the same way
```

`visit(IdentifierNode*)`'s unbound arm was a comment saying a later stage
would answer; nothing could - the writing scope is the only place the
answer is knowable - and sema reported the name after every lookup of its
own had failed.  Now `refuse_unbound_name` reports it: E0202 when the
enclosing call's visit marked the identifier as its callee (`callee_ident`,
set for the callee's own visit and cleared for the arguments), E0201
otherwise.  E0202 carries the parse note (`generic_angle_guessed`), the
owners of the leaf (`module_declarers_of_leaf`: every module whose scope
declares a function or intrinsic under it - byte-identical to sema's note
on the three allocator leaves) or, failing those, a did-you-mean over the
functions the writer can see by a bare name (`visible_function_names`,
the rib chain's own functions and its imports followed to a function);
E0201 a did-you-mean over the locals and parameters of the enclosing
function (`visible_local_names`).  Sema's collectors go with the move:
`collect_bare_callable_names` read `callable_names`, which held only
qualified keys and was filtered to bare ones, so it was empty by
construction - the known "E0202 did-you-mean's empty population", which
dissolves rather than being fixed; the population is now the visible one.

Sema's two reports are `require` doors: a `Pending` slot records a bug
and returns `Err`; `Err` returns silently; anything else bound to nothing
callable or valued is the residual E0201/E0202, without the notes that
only an unbound name earns.

#### What the probe found the name layer was not binding

Probe (`scripts/ns-migration/8.249/probe_unbound.py`; every miss of the

were unbound on GREEN programs, the population a refusal would break:

The reporting move alone broke two projects: `visibility_gate` and

analysis continues past resolution errors, with `Err` poisoning

### 8.253 The lane gate's store rule reads the tree: a store is a type that owns a map, every map owner is a store with rows or an exclusion with a reason, and one in neither refuses the run - §8.241's rule was a hand-written list of seven the script never checked, audit 13 added a map-keyed member to the context and it read OK, and the rule's first run over the real tree found the store the list had missed, `DefaultRegistry`, which carries a live bug; six self-test mutations, the pair re-runnable; D28 recorded - 2026-09-18

> **Status:** LANDED.  `scripts/lane-gate.py` rule 1 rewritten (`STORES` +
> `EXCLUDED`, `place_map_owners`, `--names` prints the population);
> `tests/lane-baseline.txt` re-pinned at 19 buckets (`DEFAULT_READ` 0,
> `DEFAULT_WRITE` 0; `LOOKUP_LOCAL` 60 → 57); `scripts/lane-gate-selftest.py`
> 17 → 23 mutations, its fixture's exclusion stubs generated from the gate's
> table; `scripts/ns-migration/8.253/pair.py` runs the old gate and the new
> over the audit's mutation.  §0: D28 added (RULED - UNBUILT, Jake's ruling
> of 2026-09-18, both checks verified at `7239982f`), the `DefaultRegistry`
> row, the exclusions row, the `lane-check` and `lane-selftest` rows, three
> bucket-count checks 17 → 19; §5.2 and §7 said eighteen beside checks that
> read 17 (audit 13) and say nineteen beside checks that read 19; §8.241's
> false sentence corrected in place with a pointer here.  No compiler
> source changed.

#### Why

Audit 13's headline: §8.241's first rule - *a store is a declaration-holding
type the `CompilationContext` carries* - was the ledger's sentence and not
the script's.  The script held `STORES`, a dict of seven typed by hand, and
never read the context's fields; the sentence *"the next type added to the
context is a question the script asks"* described a check that did not
exist.  The audit proved it the only way a gate is ever proved: a new
pointer member on the context, its type owning a map keyed by a `SymbolStr`
id, a reader and a caller - and `lane-gate` printed `OK`.  That is the same
hole as the `lookup_*` name pattern §8.230 removed and the receiver
spellings §8.241 removed, one rule further up: a list is a hole wherever it
stands in for a definition.

#### The rule

**A store is a type that owns a map.**  Rule 1's candidate test is a field
of the tree's one map type, `HashMap<K, V>` (or `HashSet<T>`, its set form;
no field today), in any `type` block, read from the tree on every run.  The
key type is deliberately not consulted.  No map in this tree is declared
`HashMap<SymbolStr, …>`: a name keys a map by its interned id (`DefId`'s
own comment: "the maps it keys are `HashMap<u32, TypeRef>` on
`SymbolStr.id`"), and a `u64` key is two of them packed (`method_returns`),
a type id (`type_index`) or a source position (`ResolutionMap::make_key`),
so the key's spelling cannot separate a name-keyed table from a
position-keyed one and a rule that pretended to would be a list of key
spellings.  Instead every owner is PLACED: as a store, with the rows its
reads and writes land in (`STORES`), or as an exclusion, with the reason its
key names no declaration (`EXCLUDED`).  A map owner in neither table
refuses the run and names itself; so does a listed type that owns no map (a
stale entry, the table drifting from the tree the way the old list had) or
one declared with a map in a file the table does not name (a second
`ConstantTable` elsewhere would otherwise be placed by the first's row).
`TypeUtils` is the one store with no map, sema's funnel in front of the
index, marked `funnel=True`; a funnel given a map is refused too, because a
funnel holds nothing.

The population, as the tree gives it (`python scripts/lane-gate.py --names`):
**22 map owners** - 7 stores (`DeclarationIndex` 13 maps, `GenericRegistry`

#### What the rule found

The first run over the real tree refused it:

```
`DefaultRegistry` (compiler/passes/default_expansion.cryo) owns a map (name_index: HashMap<u32>) and is in neither STORES nor EXCLUDED
```

`DefaultRegistry` is a declaration store keyed by the template's BARE leaf
(`TemplateEntry.name` - "Unqualified: `Array`"), built on the default-
expansion pass's stack, threaded through it as a parameter,
first-registered-wins, fed from the process-global `GenericRegistry`
regardless of what the module imports.  It is a store by the rule and by
what it does, so it has rows: `DEFAULT_READ` / `DEFAULT_WRITE`, both **0**,
because the store and its only reader share one file and a store's own
calls are not the surface.  Predicted before the run: buckets 17 → 19, both
new rows 0, `LOOKUP_LOCAL` 60 → 57 (the three calls on a `DefaultRegistry*`
parameter - `reg.lookup` ×2, `reg.register` ×1 - had been counted as local
because the receiver's type was not a store; now they are the store's own),
nothing else moving.  Measured exactly that.

What the rows pin is that the store EXISTS and that no other stage reaches
it - not how its own pass reads it.  That is a stated limit of "a store's
own file is excluded", and it matters here because the store carries a live
bug the gate cannot see: the rewrite site copies the annotation's stamp
across (`old_res`) and then matches by written spelling
(`reg.lookup(named.name)`), so an import that binds nothing poisons an
unrelated same-leaf type:

```cryo
import std::fs::path;      // binds nothing (D7), but brings the module in
struct PathBuf { n: i32 }  // the user's own, non-generic
const p: PathBuf = PathBuf { n: 1 };
p.n                        // E0204 no field or method `n` on type Main::PathBuf
```

Remove the import and it compiles.  Refused by `7239982f` and by the pin
`db5af63c` alike.  The stamp is present and ignored; reading it is the next
unit, and the row says so.

### 8.254 Default expansion asks the stamp: a bare reference is expanded when its `Res` names a template whose every parameter has a default (`template_of(def)`), the enclosing declarations are held by `DefId`, and the pass's own store - all-default templates keyed by BARE leaf, fed from the process-global registry regardless of imports, matched by spelling with the stamp copied across and ignored - is deleted with both collectors; the name layer stamps the `static match` scrutinee it had left for the type resolver, which was every Pending slot at the site on a green program, so both rewrite sites are D23 doors; the poisoning import is pinned as a project; 0 disagreements and 0 objects moved over the six halves - 2026-09-18

> **Status:** LANDED.  `passes/default_expansion.cryo`: `DefaultRegistry`,
> `DefaultEntry`, `collect_local_defaults`, `collect_cross_module_defaults`,
> `register_if_all_default` deleted; `ScopeStack` holds `DefId`s; `defaults_of(d,
> registry)`; the named annotation's site reads `named.res.require(...)`, the
> scope segment's `require_scope_res(...)`; every `rewrite_*` takes the
> `GenericRegistry*`.  `resolver/name_resolution.cryo`: `visit(StaticMatchExprNode*)`
> and `visit(StaticMatchStmtNode*)` stamp `node.scrutinee`.  New project
> `tests/tests/projects/default_expansion_by_stamp` (roster merged, 68).
> `lane-gate.py`: the `DefaultRegistry` store and its two rows retired (17
> buckets), and a golden section no bucket counts is refused; the self-test
> checks that refusal.  §0: the `DefaultRegistry` row DELETED with checks,
> D23's two door counts, the exclusions row (21 owners, 6 stores), the
> `lane-check`, `lane-selftest`, `make test` rows, the bucket checks 19 → 17,
> the roster check 68.

#### Why

§8.253's rule found the store and named the bug; this entry removes both.
The pass's question was "is this spelling the name of an all-default
template?", asked of a table built per pass from every template the process
had registered - so a module that imported `std::fs::path` (binding nothing,
D7) and declared its own non-generic `PathBuf` had every `PathBuf` it wrote
rewritten to `PathBuf<GlobalAlloc>`, and `p.n` was E0204.  The stamp beside
the spelling already said which `PathBuf` it was; the pass copied it across
to the node it built and never read it.

What Rust does: default type arguments are applied by `hir_ty_lowering`
when a path has RESOLVED to a definition with generics - by the `DefId`,
never by a per-pass name table.  So here.

#### The change

```cryo
// before: a per-pass table keyed by the template's bare leaf
if (scope.contains(named.name)) { return; }          // the enclosing declarations, by NAME
const entry: DefaultEntry* = reg.lookup(named.name); // first-registered-wins, every module's templates
if (entry == null) { return; }
// after: the stamp names the definition; the registry answers by it
const d: DefId = named.res.require("default_expansion:named annotation").def_id();
if (!d.is_valid() || scope.contains(d)) { return; }  // the enclosing declarations, by DefId
const defaults: TypeAnnotation*[] = DefaultExpansionPasses::defaults_of(d, reg);
if (defaults.length == 0) { return; }
```

`defaults_of` is `template_of(d)` → `get_generic_params()` → every parameter
has a default → one deep clone per parameter, at the site.  The scope
segment (`String::from_str`) reads `TypeRelative(Def(d), _)` off
`require_scope_res` and does the same.  Three things the name stack did are
not needed by identity: a generic parameter of a function or an impl block
was pushed so a global template spelled the same would not be matched - its
stamp is `GenericParam`, which names no template; the local collector
existed because the pass "runs before the current module's templates are
registered" - `register_templates` has run over every module before any
module's DefaultExpansion since the driver was reshaped, and the
cross-module collector already pulled the local module's entries too; and
first-registered-wins was the tie-break for two templates sharing a leaf,
which a `DefId` cannot have.

**The scrutinee.**  `require` at the named site reports E0900 on a green
build for every Pending slot, so the Pending population decides whether the
site can be a door (§8.248's standard).  Measured with the probe
(`scripts/ns-migration/8.254/shadow.py --invert`, over the OLD pass: prints
`DEFEXP-PENDING` on every unstamped slot at either site, `DEFEXP-CTL` on
every agreement) over `corpus2.sh Y2p` (`.objcmp/y2p-corpus.out`,
`.objcmp/Y2p-lines.txt`): **2,531 Pending**, of which **2,517 are `T` in
`static match (T)`** - `visit(StaticMatchExprNode*)` stamped each arm's
patterns and left the scrutinee "for the TypeResolver" - and 14 are
undeclared names on refused programs (`Nope`, `NoSuchMod::Inner::Widget`,
`bool`, …: 8 negatives, 4 `compile_fail` projects), where `require`'s record
is silent because the build has errors.  `old=1` on a Pending slot: **0**.
The scrutinee is a written type and is stamped like the patterns now; the
site is a door.

> eighth session's handoff.  `scripts/ns-migration/8.256/probe_d18.py`
> (the two instruments, reverted from the tree); unit

> test` row.

#### What changed for a program

This is a **language behaviour change**, not a requalification, and it
is the one Jake chose (§8.216): the alias keyword folds rather than the
arm being deleted.  Before, `int` in a name position was a spelling the
name layer left `Pending` (a module may own the name - `std::fmt::float`
does - so `is_primitive_spelling` refused to answer it) and every
consumer carried a spelling arm for exactly that population:

```cryo
type trait Show { show(&this) -> i32; }
implement trait Show for int { show(&this) -> i32 { return *this * 2; } }

const a: i32 = 21;   a.show();     // E0358 before: the head was keyed "int", no receiver asks it
const b: int = 4;    b.show();     // E0358 before, and E0201 inside the body: `this` unbound
int::try_from(big)                 // E0636 before: reached codegen unresolved
```

All three compile now (`a.show()` is 42, `b.show()` 8, `int::try_from(40)`
is `Ok(40)`), because the stamp is `PrimTy("i32")` - never
`PrimTy("int")`: one type, one key, wherever a stamp is read.  The fold
is asked at exactly two places and only after every scope has declined
the name (`type_spelling_res`'s bare leaf after `leaf_in_module_scope`,
the scope segment's `!have_base` tail), which is Rust's rule for a
primitive name and what makes a module named like one win while it is
in scope: `float::parse_f64` with `std::fmt::float` imported is the
module, unchanged.  A mutant that folds BEFORE the scope walk refuses
the unit's module case with `E0233: cannot find float::parse_f64`
(built, run, reverted).  Under HEAD's compiler the unit file is refused
with E0201 + E0358 ×2 (`cryo check`, which stops before the E0636);
under the tree it passes (3 of 3).

E0308's coherence check still collides `for int` with `for i32`
(`E0308_primitive_alias_duplicate` unchanged, at line 14, `for type
i32`): the head arm that substituted `PrimTy(<spelling>)` for a source
head with a key and no stamp is `node.res.require("type_resolution:
coherence head")` now - a source head with a key IS a stamped head,
since every written target the name layer can bind is stamped and a
head it cannot bind has no key and skips the check; only a clone
carries a key with no stamp, and clones are not source declarations.

#### One home for the alias table

`ResBase::is_alias_keyword` (names only) is `ResBase::primitive_of_alias`
(name → the primitive's spelling, or ""), and the three other copies go:
`types/resolver.cryo`'s `resolve_primitive` folds through it and drops
its four alias arms; `const_table.cryo`'s two annotation-text readers
(`declares_integer`, `primitive_name_of` → `wrap_to_primitive`) fold
through `ConstantTable::keyword_primitive` and drop theirs;
`sema/helpers.cryo`'s `is_numeric_type_name` drops an `int` arm that
read an arena display name, which never held the alias.  `ann_canon_key`'s
keyword arm folds a `TypeAnnotation::Primitive` lexeme before minting its
`PrimTy`, so `Feed<int>` and `Feed<i32>` render to one coherence key
without the index holding a key for `int`.

#### The two deletions, measured

`probe_d18.py` over `corpus2.sh Z1p` with the fold in place
(`.objcmp/z1p-corpus.out`: lsp direct exit 0, `OVERALL PASS … 194 … 65`,
`failing halves: 0`; `.objcmp/Z1p-lines.txt`, 1,407 lines):

| instrument | fold in place | HEAD + the same probe (control) |
|---|---|---|
| `NEW-SPELLING`: sema's `new` answered by `lookup_type_exact(type_name)` and not the stamp | **0** | 2 (`new_array.cryo:22` `int`, twice) |
| `NEW-STAMPED`: the stamp answered (control) | 1,407, `new_array.cryo:22 int` ×2 among them | — |
| `ALIASREAD`: `DeclarationIndex::lookup_type` asked for one of the four forward-only alias ids | **0** | 112 on `new_array.cryo`, 54 on the E0308 negative |

So sema's `new` spelling step (the shadow) and the four
`register_type_forward_only` registrations (with the method, which had no

The control column is the same instrument over HEAD's sources (the fold

#### The alias-vs-member split

Five prints, one per site that reads a written `alias::member` spelling
where a stamp should have answered, over `corpus2.sh Q1p`
(`.objcmp/q1p-corpus.out`: lsp direct exit 0, `OVERALL PASS … 194 … 65`,
`failing halves: 0`; `.objcmp/Q1p-lines.txt`, 3,047 lines):

| group | site | lines | what |
|---|---|---|---|
| alias | `QUAL-TYPE` | 1,078 | `scope_qualifier_type` read `TypeRelative(Def(<module>::alias))` and the index held no type for it: `compiler::codegen::llvm` 1,004 (the LSP half builds codegen), `FfiCImport::CImportTest::cit` 51, `…::CImportLibclang::probe` 23 - the same 1,078 of §8.247's finding |
| alias | `CALL-DOOR` | 968 | `try_resolve_cimport_function` answered a call by the spelling after the type-owner doors declined: `llvm` 956, `probe` 12 |
| alias | `CALL-HINT` | 968 | the callee hint's `lookup_func_type_exact(bare_sym)`: the same 968 |
| alias | `CG-VALUE` | 22 | codegen's scope-resolution value with no module stamp, `resolve_global("<alias>::<member>")`: `cit` 17, `probe` 5 - every constant use |
| member | `TYPE-LEAF` | 11 | a qualified type spelling answered from the writer's own module scope as a whole-spelling symbol: `cit::Vec2` ×2, `cit::Value` ×3, `Bits`, `Celsius`, `Named`, `NeverS`, `NeverU`, `Tagged` |

The alias group is every function call and every constant read under
the three aliases; the member group is the C-import TYPES, which the
name layer declares whole (`declare_c_imported_type`, `cit::Vec2` as one
symbol with no module) and answers without asking what `cit` is.  The
scope segment's answer today is the leak: `cit` binds in scope to a
`Namespace` symbol, the segment site takes any bound non-parameter as a
`Def` base, and nothing after it asks whether the symbol names a type, so
the stamp `TypeRelative(Def(<module>::cit), 1)` claims a type that does
not exist and every consumer falls to the spelling.

So: a stamp `Def(<declaring module>::alias)` - the scope segment
dispatching on the bound symbol's kind, as it does for a generic
parameter - closes the alias group through the doors a module's members
already use (`resolve_module_qualified_symbol`, `resolve_global_in_namespace`)
**if** the key space moves with it: extern functions from `alias::name`
to `<mod>::alias::name`, C-import types and globals likewise (the
importer's `binding_namespace` carrying the canonical namespace, the
global slot keyed `(leaf, ns)` as every other global is, which collapses
`decl_global_key`'s binding branch), the C linker symbol untouched.  The
member group then answers from the alias's module scope by the module
lane, and `declare_c_imported_type` goes.

### 8.259 Q2 built as a resolver module: an `extern module` alias is a module of the resolver's own under the canonical namespace `<declaring module>::alias`, its functions, types and constants declared and exported there and keyed by it, the alias symbol's qualified name IS that namespace, and every consumer reads a `Def(<mod>::alias)` stamp through the doors a graph module's members use - the scope segment, the type spelling, the call, the constant, the codegen value; the C-import key space `alias::X`, codegen's global ladder, the call resolver's C-import door and its callee hint's spelling door, sema's alias-global read, the index's bare-leaf global map and the whole-spelling type declaration are deleted; no graph loop touched; 518 alias answers over the six halves, 0 misses, 0 objects moved outside the two C-import users, whose 15 constants are mangled under their module - 2026-09-19
